At a glance

3,000–7,000+

Detained in Delhi today (media)

Context & sources

The Hindu (6:53 PM) restates that over 5,000 protesters were detained in Delhi, including CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, CPI(M) leaders and student activists. Delhi Police said at 6:53 PM they have begun releasing detainees (a senior officer via The Hindu); no count of releases given.

NDTV (7:41 PM, with PTI inputs): over 1,500 detained across Delhi; many were released later in the evening. Scroll (8:16 PM): police reportedly detained more than 7,000 protesters in Delhi. NDTV (~10 PM): at least 3,000 detained across Delhi; most released by night.

Delhi Police sources via ANI (9:38 PM): all detainees released from detention centres except CJP leaders, for whom due legal process will be followed. As of 10:05 PM. ThePrint (5:28 PM): around 3,500 detained in Delhi; police say detentions could last 'up to 24 hours'.

Officials told PTI at 4:53 PM that Delhi Police detained over 3,000 people during the protest (The Hindu's summary says 3,300; The Tribune says 3,000). A Delhi Police officer told The Hindu around 5,000 were detained till 2 PM. TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee claimed (ANI, ~5:07 PM) about 2,500 were detained.

A Delhi Police officer told The Hindu around 5,000 protesters were detained across Delhi till 2 PM and taken to temporary detention facilities (The Hindu live blog, 2:57 PM entry; Scroll repeated it at ~4:45 PM). Earlier figures: TOI 1,500+ (midday); PTI citing police sources ~1,000 (3:57 PM).

Outside Delhi: Chennai 100+ (NDTV, ~4:22 PM); Bengaluru at least 50 AISA students at Freedom Park (The Hindu, 3:21 PM); Mumbai: over 400 detained so far at August Kranti Maidan (Mumbai Police via ANI, 5:39 PM;

PTI had ~200 at 5:18 PM); actor Imran Khan and his relative Zayn Marie Khan were among those detained (NDTV, 8:30 PM); Pune: about 80–100 detained at Lal Mahal Chowk and taken to Lashkar police station (IANS, 8:46 PM); earlier Scroll reported detentions with no number. HT (10:47 PM): police say nearly 4,000 detained.

As of 11:10 PM. NDTV (12:12 AM headline): at least 3,000 were detained in Delhi and all of them were released except the CJP leaders and Dhruv Rathee. NDTV also reports at least 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed. As of 12:15 AM. Over 7,000 released per police sources (DNA, 8:00 AM;

ET Now, ~7:19 AM). ET Now says all 7,000 were released except Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee and two others. DNA, citing police sources, says Dipke and Das remain in custody.

CJP claims more than 15,000 people, including students, civil society members and political leaders, faced detention and police action (Indian Express; CJP claim). Police sources told Indian Express that detainees were kept at around 30 detention centres. As of 8:15 AM.

Correction, 10:05 AM: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released at about 10 AM on an Executive Magistrate's order (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). Dhruv Rathee was released at about 3 AM (Hindustan Times, PTI). That corrects the morning reports that still had them in custody. As of 10:05 AM.

HT (11:40 AM, 11 Oct): an estimated 7,000 people were detained on Saturday. As of 12:05 PM. 11 Oct: about 60–70 people were detained at Connaught Place (Indian Express, 12:28 PM), and The Hindu reported student activists detained there later. No official count for Sunday. As of 2:05 PM.

Police sources, via The Hindu (3:38 PM, 11 Oct), say over 7,000 protesters were detained on Saturday as authorities stopped people reaching Jantar Mantar. Attributed to police sources, not an official figure.

Hindustan Times (3:24 PM): about 100 more protesters were packed into two buses and removed from Connaught Place, and detentions there continued despite the Supreme Court order. HT also says more than 26,000 security personnel were deployed alongside Delhi Police. As of 4:05 PM.

PTI (4:08 PM): more than 100 people were detained in Delhi on Sunday while marching toward Jantar Mantar. Tribune/PTI (5:46 PM): dozens, including Anjali Damania, were detained at Shivaji Park in Mumbai, and about 600 people had been detained in Mumbai on Saturday.

AAP's Sanjay Singh claims more than 6,000 people were detained in Delhi on Saturday (PTI, 4:57 PM). His claim. As of 6:10 PM. Sunday evening: Indian Express reported many fresh detentions at Connaught Place, including women held in large numbers near Rajiv Chowk Metro Gate 7. No official count for Sunday evening.

As of 8:10 PM. Goa: Times of India (7:16 PM) and The Hindu/PTI reported dozens detained at Azad Maidan, including CJP leader Amreen Shaikh. The Bombay High Court (Goa bench) later ordered those Panaji detainees released.

Times of India and The Goan name seven: Jack Sukhija, Amreen Shaikh (Times of India spells the name Afreen), Aditya Parulekar, Bhupesh Bind, Liston Noronha, Shamiro or Shamino Fernandes, and Milind Rane. PTI and India Today say six. Both counts are kept. The Goan says they were released around 9:40 PM.

As of 6:00 AM, 12 Oct. 14 Oct, fifth day: The Hindu (published 11:00 PM) reported that hundreds took to central Delhi streets. SFI and DYFI marched on Firoz Shah Road. Police, including Delhi Police, the RAF and the CRPF, detained protesters sitting on the road.

The Hindu said several were "pushed and bundled" into vehicles. The Indian Youth Congress marched from Patel Chowk metro along Ashoka Road and was stopped near Parliament Street police station. Protesters were detained. Police cited BNSS Sec 163. The number detained was not released by police.

Traffic was disrupted in the New Delhi district.

No official count

Released today

Context & sources

A group of lawyers detained near the Supreme Court were released after the CJI stepped in (about 2:30 PM). Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat was released (Bar & Bench, 6:51 PM). Pinarayi Vijayan was released (PTI, ~7:10 PM).

ANI reported Ratna Singh's release at about 5:53 PM, but The Hindu says she posted at 7:13 PM that she was still detained; the reports conflict. 6:53 PM: Delhi Police say they have initiated the release of protesters (a senior officer via The Hindu); no count given.

7:11 PM: women released from Maidan Garhi police station (The Wire). 7:38 PM: police sources say women and senior citizens are being released first (The Hindu); many detainees were released in the evening (NDTV). 8:09 PM: Mamata Banerjee released (ANI).

8:13 PM: Arvind Kejriwal released from Jaffarpur police station (PTI). 8:30 PM: Neha Bora and the women detained with her released from Maidan Garhi police station (India Today). No overall release count given. 9:18 PM: police sources say most of those detained today have been released (IANS).

9:38 PM: Delhi Police sources say all detainees were released from detention centres except CJP leaders (ANI). 9:20 PM: Pinarayi Vijayan, John Brittas and K.N. Balagopal released from Mandir Marg police station (IANS). 9:35 PM: Yogendra Yadav says he was released from Maidangarhi police station (his own post).

9:59 PM: about 150 people picked up from Gurudwara Bangla Sahib were released from Chhatrasal Stadium (Scroll). No overall release count given. 11 Oct: Dhruv Rathee released at about 3 AM and handed to his family (Hindustan Times, PTI, citing officials).

Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka released at about 10 AM on an Executive Magistrate's order at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, citing Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench). 14 Oct: the Special Executive Magistrate at Mandir Marg released Ajinkya Shinde on a personal bond of Rs 5,000 (Indian Express; ABP Live).

Abhijeet Dipke (X, via Moneycontrol) said the 11 other CJP activists detained with them were released: "Welcome back team." His post. Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were not released. They were remanded to Tihar.

Two in Tihar

Named key figures still held

Context & sources

Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released at about 10 AM on 11 Oct on an Executive Magistrate's order at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:58 AM, citing Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench, 10:00 AM).

Dhruv Rathee was released at about 3 AM and handed to his family (Hindustan Times and PTI, citing officials). This corrects earlier "still in custody" reports, including ETV Bharat, ET Now and this page's 8:15 AM update. Senior Advocate Dinesh Dwivedi: no new report.

Ratna Singh was at the production as CJP's lawyer; an outlet has not confirmed when her own detention ended. Fidal Tom and students Saurabh, Nikhil and Harsh were released overnight (The Wire). The earlier "at least 12" figure counted named people whose individual status was already unconfirmed or likely released.

As of 10:05 AM IST. The three were released on a one-year condition that they not breach the peace, with a Rs 50,000 surety, according to LiveLaw citing Ratna Singh, PTI, and Delhi Police via ANI. Dhruv Rathee later said he was kidnapped and gave no undertaking (Hindustan Times, his claim).

The Hindu says he was released around 2 AM; HT and PTI say about 3 AM. As of 12:05 PM IST. John Brittas was detained again at about 1 PM on 11 Oct at Connaught Place (Indian Express). Dipke is travelling home to Hingoli; his family says a police delay made him miss his grandmother's funeral, and police dispute that.

Das and Ranka were due at a 2 PM press conference. As of 2:05 PM IST. Neha Bora was detained again at about 3:50 PM on 11 Oct while leading a march to Connaught Place (ThePrint, Scroll). John Brittas was later released; CPI(M) alleges police assaulted him and left him injured (ThePrint, India Today).

Ratna Singh is now confirmed released; she spoke at the Press Club press conference (The Hindu, 3:38 PM). Three Indian Express Hindi reporters were detained at Connaught Place, and two phones were seized (Indian Express, 3:57 PM). As of 4:05 PM IST.

The three Indian Express Hindi reporters were released about 45 minutes later (Indian Express, 4:14 PM). Neha Bora was still reported detained as of 6:10 PM, with no release report. Anjali Damania was detained at about 4:50 PM at Shivaji Park, Mumbai (PTI). As of 6:10 PM IST.

As of 8:10 PM, Neha Bora and Anjali Damania were still reported detained, with no release report for either. Dipke missed his grandmother's funeral and flew to Nagpur on the way to Hingoli. His uncle says the release came too late; police deny a delay.

As of 10:10 PM, Neha Bora and Anjali Damania were still reported detained. Amreen Shaikh was detained at Azad Maidan and released around 9:40 PM on 11 Oct on a Bombay High Court (Goa bench) order (The Goan; PTI; Times of India). Dipke says he signed no bond against protesting;

Ratna Singh's earlier account, via LiveLaw, is a one-year no-breach-of-peace condition. Both are kept. As of 6:00 AM on 12 Oct, Neha Bora's release is still unconfirmed. Sudhir Sangwan and Balakrishnan Shukla: whereabouts unknown per CJP. Dipke is in Hingoli.

As of 9:35 PM on 12 Oct, Dhruv Rathee's Monday claim of unofficial house arrest, in an India Today report updated at 12:16 PM from The Lallantop, is his claim. No police confirmation was found. He remains listed as released on 11 Oct.

As of 9:15 PM on 13 Oct, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde were still held after the morning detention. ANI (about 8:47 PM) said Delhi Police registered a case against Das, Ranka and others for unauthorised trespassing at Jantar Mantar. No penal section was confirmed. No release was reported.

As of 9:00 AM on 15 Oct, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are in Tihar Jail on five days' judicial custody from 14 Oct (Indian Express; The Hindu, updated 12:16 AM on 15 Oct; BBC, about 9:55 AM on 14 Oct; AP). India Today says Das is in Jail No. 2 and Ranka in Jail No. 4, as undertrials after medical checks.

Ajinkya Shinde was released the same morning on a personal bond. Dipke said 11 others were released. A Patiala House bail move for Das and Ranka was reported (India Today video, 1:07 PM). No bail order as of 9:00 AM. Dhruv Rathee remains listed as released on 11 Oct.

On 14 Oct a Delhi court issued fresh summons in a 2018 defamation case over his "BJP IT Cell" video. The next hearing is 17 Oct (NDTV; New Indian Express). That case is separate from the protest. ThePrint reports his claim that Delhi Police are following him in unmarked cars. His claim.

No police confirmation was found. As of 9:00 PM IST on 15 Oct, no bail order was reported for Saurav Das or Ashutosh Ranka. They remain in Tihar on the five days' judicial custody from 14 Oct. Times of India says the Special Executive Magistrate matter is still listed for further inquiry on 19 Oct.

The Patiala House bail move reported on 14 Oct had no grant or rejection in the reports used here. Ajinkya Shinde remains released on a personal bond. No new detention of Abhijeet Dipke was reported.

Very important15 Oct, 8:38 PMIST

The Hindu / PTI (8:38 PM): Delhi Police urged people to stay away from CJP's proposed Lehra Do Tiranga march at Connaught Place on Friday, but said it could facilitate a select group to wave the national flag and sing the national anthem at a suitable place. The statement cited BNSS Sec 163 already in force in Connaught Place and adjoining areas, to keep the peace and protect life and property. A limited number of people could be allowed for what police called a symbolic display. That is the police statement. It is not a grant of Dipke's open call, and it is not a court order permitting the march. It sits beside the High Court's refusal to restrain the gathering and beside NDMC's closure of Central Park.

Very important15 Oct, 7:37 PMIST

PTI via The Hindu (7:37 PM) and ThePrint: the New Delhi Municipal Council said Central Park, Connaught Place, will remain closed to the general public on 16 and 17 Oct for "administrative reasons". The notice is dated 15 Oct. The Hindu and ThePrint place the closure ahead of CJP's Lehra Do Tiranga call. Hindustan Times also reported the closure. The closure is the civic body's notice. It is not itself a court ban on the call. The High Court had, earlier in the afternoon, refused to restrain the gathering and recorded the police assurance that it would be regulated.

Very important15 Oct, 4:44 PMIST

Delhi High Court, Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma (The Hindu live, 4:44 PM and 5:03 PM; The Hindu article published 8:31 PM; India Today): the court refused to restrain CJP and Abhijeet Dipke from the proposed 16 Oct protest at Central Park, Connaught Place. It did not grant express permission. The plea was by a Palika Bazar street vendor. The Hindu names senior advocate Sachhin Puri for a licensed readymade-garment vendor. He argued Connaught Place is not a designated protest site and that festive-season trade would be hit. India Today: the vendor sought regulation of the protest under Supreme Court law. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma told the court that steps had already been taken to control CJP's activities, that all possible legal measures would be used to regulate and control the gathering, and that the petitioner's concerns would be addressed. The court took that assurance on record. When the petitioner's counsel pressed for a specific restrain order, the bench said, "Don't insist. We have passed the order." India Today: the matter is listed for further consideration on 3 Nov 2026. The refusal to restrain is not a permission order. The police assurance is the police account, recorded by the court.

Very important15 Oct, 1:59 PMIST

Justice Joymalya Bagchi, wrapping up at about 1:59 PM (The Hindu, Krishnadas Rajagopal): "We have issued notices on all the petitions. Union government would file its counter affidavit. We have sought from the Union government the reasons and circumstances behind the prohibitory orders under S. 163 BNSS. We have sought the Union government's response to petitions alleging police assault on people, particularly protesters, lawyers and journalists. As far as the Delhi Union of Journalists' petition on seizure of journalists' devices, the SG has said there were no such seizures. We have asked him to make good this statement in the counter affidavit." The assault allegations are the petitioners' claims. The Solicitor General's denial of device seizures is his statement, still to be put in the counter. Earlier in the hearing he had said, on who counts as a journalist, "In our experience, any person having a mobile phone is a journalist" (Indian Express). The Chief Justice said, "Everybody acting as journalists will create problems," and that the harassment instances cited by the Network of Women in Media, India, should be investigated (The Hindu, 1:33 PM). Senior advocate Indira Jaising, for NWMI, said police cannot investigate themselves and sought a committee. The Hindu: the Chief Justice prima facie agreed to a committee whose members and chairperson are all women, and asked Ms Jaising to suggest names in a sealed cover. She had also referred to a woman judge as chair, in line with the Vishaka guidelines. The court said no coercive action should be taken against the woman journalist booked by Delhi Police after she alleged harassment. The Hindu describes that case as a booking following allegations that she publicly humiliated officers and used casteist slurs. Jaising's account, as Indian Express reported it, is that she was booked under the SC/ST Atrocities Act after accusing an assistant commissioner of sexual harassment, and that her own complaint was not registered. Both descriptions are kept. Justice Bagchi said the court will examine whether freedom of expression means every citizen can claim to be a journalist. The Hindu (1:08 PM): notice also on Bhanu Sanoriya's plea, argued by senior advocate A.N.S. Nadkarni, that protest organisers take personal responsibility for harm to others. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan said that prayer cuts both ways and that the police must also be accountable. Indian Express reported the same exchange with the Solicitor General, including responsibility for the Police Commissioner. The court also agreed to hear street vendors' compensation pleas. A lawyer told the court vendors had not earned even Rs 500 over Dussehra and Diwali. That is the lawyer's claim.

Very important15 Oct, 1:01 PMIST

The Hindu (1:01 PM): notice on a petition by Swaty Singh challenging de-notification of Jantar Mantar as a protest site. Senior advocate Mukta Gupta said protesters must be heard, and that Jantar Mantar is close to centres of power. Justice Joymalya Bagchi said advances in technology have to be kept in mind. Senior advocate N. Hariharan replied that, in that case, "we can address the court from Kerala." Indian Express names the petitioner as advocate Swaty Malik, with Mukta Gupta, a former Delhi High Court judge, and says the court asked the Union of India and the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, to file replies. NDTV Profit: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said a committee had been constituted before the decision. Indian Express: the government affidavit had tied the move to the Supreme Court's 9 Oct order. Justice Bagchi said the court needs to examine whether "oral observations" can be construed as law, and that "heard" must also be understood from the perspective of technology. Police have already named Burari Ground, Ramlila Ground (Indian Express) or Ramlila Maidan (the evening police line), and CBD Ground. Notice is not an order restoring Jantar Mantar.

Very important15 Oct, 12:59 PMIST

The Hindu (12:59 PM): the Supreme Court issued notice on a petition by Digant Mishra seeking criminal contempt against Rahul Gandhi for leading a "political procession" into the Supreme Court. Senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia, for that petition, said the attempt was to browbeat the judiciary. Chief Justice Surya Kant said "nobody can browbeat the judiciary" and that "they say something inside and something else outside." NDTV: on Bhatia's submission that the march was an attempt to pressurise the court, the Chief Justice called the attempts "feeble". "These are feeble attempts that nobody takes note of. Outside they make statements... we are not sitting in an ivory tower, we are aware of things." NDTV also reported: "Nobody can browbeat the judiciary." NDTV said notice went to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and others on a separate plea against the march, and that CCTV from the court's premises during the 12 Oct protest is to be preserved. The Hindu (1:05 PM): the bench directed preservation of CCTV footage, including in the apex court premises, after Bhatia sought preservation of the 12 Oct footage and after Kapil Sibal and Arundhati Katju raised assault allegations. Those assault allegations are the lawyers' claims.

Very important15 Oct, 12:57 PMIST

The Hindu (Krishnadas Rajagopal, 12:57 PM): Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the Supreme Court that the authorities had filed responses to the contempt notice. He said the media had misconstrued the opening paragraphs, which offer an "unqualified apology", and that this is usually a formality in a reply to a contempt notice. The affidavits go on to defend the preventive measures of 10 Oct. Indian Express and LiveLaw: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan tendered an "unconditional and unqualified apology" and said the cellular-internet suspension was a proportionate measure. He said services were suspended from 10 PM on 9 Oct to 10 PM on 10 Oct within 4 km of Raisina Hill, and that Wi-Fi and broadband were not suspended. Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar told the court the 10 Oct steps were based on intelligence and the ground situation, to prevent a disturbance of public order, and that detainees were given meals (The Hindu, 11:57 AM; Indian Express). NDTV Profit reported that the court said it was not taking cognisance of the "unqualified apology", and that an apology accompanied by justification is a qualified one. Both the apology language and the defence of the measures are kept.

Very important15 Oct, 12:55 PMIST

Supreme Court, Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi, in an hour-long hearing (Indian Express; LiveLaw, 12:55 PM): notice was issued on Rahul Gandhi's INDIA-bloc petition against the Special Intensive Revision to the Election Commission of India, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, named as a personal respondent, and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. LiveLaw also reported notice on AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi's SIR plea. When Owaisi's counsel Nizam Pasha pressed an interim prayer for production of the Commission's file notings, LiveLaw reported that the court said notice was being issued on all the prayers. That is notice, not a reported interim stay or suspension of SIR. Indian Express reported notice to the Election Commission on modification of Form 6, the form for enrolling a new voter. The Hindu's 12:59 PM live line also referred to the Digvijaya Singh and Owaisi petitions. The Chief Justice said issuing notice does not mean the conduct is condoned. Indian Express: "We have no problem with the other petitioners… We are issuing notice, but we are not condoning the conduct. Let the petitioner file an affidavit on their conduct." The petitioner was not named in that report. NDTV: "We will issue notice but we want to know his conduct on the next date of hearing." LiveLaw said similar SIR matters are scheduled for Tuesday, and that an opposition petition could be heard with the other pending SIR matters.

Very important14 Oct, 7:27 PMIST

Rahul Gandhi v Election Commission of India, the INDIA bloc leaders' writ filed on 12 Oct, is on the 15 Oct Supreme Court cause list before Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi (PTI via Deccan Herald, 7:27 PM; The Hindu; Business Today). The Hindu says Justice V. Mohana is not sitting on 15 Oct and that the regular three-judge bench "stands cancelled." Prayers, as reported from the petition: records of Election Commission decisions on the Special Intensive Revision, ECINET and ERONET access logs, an independent audit of deletions by a committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, booth-wise publication of deleted names with reasons, no deletion without notice and a hearing, and an interim suspension of SIR nationwide. India Today (published 8:04 PM, updated 8:29 PM), Bar & Bench (about 8:20 PM) and NDTV published the petition's ten prayers. In paraphrase of that prayer block: (1) the Election Commission to produce the complete files, agendas, minutes, notings and objections of the Election Commissioners on disputed SIR decisions, plus ECINET and ERONET access logs and the complete file for the 24 June 2025 decision to begin nationwide SIR; (2) examine whether those decisions complied with Article 324, Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, and T.N. Seshan v. Union of India, and quash and set aside any decision taken without lawful authority; (3) action against persons responsible for breaches, including under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, where warranted; (4) pending adjudication, every SIR-related Commission decision to be taken and minuted under Section 18; (5) online Form 6 to conform to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, unless those Rules are lawfully amended; (6) an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, with technical experts, to audit SIR deletions and database access, including ECINET and ERONET, and to review EVM policies, procedures and technical design against global best practices; (7) booth-wise publication of deleted electors with reasons and a gender and age breakdown, and a working way to restore eligible names; (8) no deletion without notice and a hearing, and eligible persons in Punjab and other poll-bound States allowed to seek inclusion until the last date the law allows; (9) an interim direction suspending the ongoing SIR across States pending adjudication; (10) other orders the court finds fit. The published prayer block does not ask for the Chief Election Commissioner's removal. India Today's introduction describes the plea as challenging the validity of SIR. The petition text in the same story says it does not seek to reopen the validity of SIR after the court's 27 May 2026 judgment in ADR v ECI. It challenges implementation and whether the Commission acted as a collective institution. The petition cites an Indian Express report of 23 September 2026 that the two Election Commissioners had recorded objections. It notes that the Commission says differences are normal and that decisions were unanimous. Both accounts are kept.

Satheesan moved it. The House took it up from about 12:52 PM and it had passed by about 1:29 PM. UDF and LDF supported it. The BJP objected and proposed amendments that were rejected. The resolution seeks Kumar's removal, steps to improve the Election Commission's transparency, action by the Centre and the Commission on defects in the Special Intensive Revision, restoration of voting rights to eligible voters wrongly excluded, and a selection panel that again includes the Chief Justice of India alongside the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition, citing an earlier Supreme Court order. Satheesan accepted Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan's amendment changing "lakhs" of excluded voters to "crores". A state Assembly resolution is not binding. Under Article 324(5) a Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge, by a special-majority motion in Parliament. The Bombay High Court (Goa bench) ordered the release of CJP activists detained at Azad Maidan in Panaji. Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar held a special Sunday-evening hearing on habeas corpus pleas by Melisa Simoes and Rui Gomes Pereira. Senior Advocate Norma Alvares appeared with Om D'Costa. Alvares, via PTI, said the hearing ran from about 7:30 PM to 8:45 PM. Times of India quotes the court: "Considering that there are no prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, we are of the opinion that the detention may not have been authorised." The bench was told an executive magistrate gave oral instructions to detain them because they "barged into" Azad Maidan. The court did not rule on whether the detention was correct. The public prosecutor assured the court they would be released. Alvares gave an undertaking that they would not protest at Azad Maidan on Sunday night only. The Goan: they were released around 9:40 PM from Panaji police station after a bus brought them back from Pernem police station. Times of India and The Goan name seven: Jack Sukhija, Amreen Shaikh (Times of India spells the name Afreen), Aditya Parulekar, Bhupesh Bind, Liston Noronha, Shamiro or Shamino Fernandes, and Milind Rane. PTI and India Today say six. Both counts are kept. The court ordered the Panaji and Pernem station in-charges to file affidavits on the reasons for the detention and on why the peaceful protest was not allowed. Further hearing Monday 12 Oct at noon (The Goan). A medical exam at Goa Medical College was offered because two were reportedly injured (Alvares). Alvares also argued that Shaikh, a woman, could not be detained after 6 PM (Times of India). Jack Sukhija, after release, told PTI that phones were taken away and they were not allowed to contact anyone. His claim. This confirms the 9:09 PM post by TOI journalist Bindiya Chari. PTI reported it at 11:22 PM, India Today at 10:50 PM, and New Indian Express at 11:16 PM.

Indian Express (12:25 AM), reporting what it learnt: the Chief Justice's reply made four points. Under the constitutional scheme the court cannot take cognisance of such grievances on the administrative side. The court has judicial review powers under Article 32, and if a petition is filed on Monday it will be taken up the following day, Tuesday 13 Oct, when the already pending matters are listed. The court is committed to fundamental rights and its doors are always open. The march is still set for 1:30 PM from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba Road junction to the Supreme Court, about 2 km.

Very important11 Oct, 5:25 PMIST

The Supreme Court's written order is out. LiveLaw and Bar & Bench: the court finds a prima facie case of contempt over the Metro and train shutdown, treated as a violation of its 9 Oct order. Notice went to the alleged contemnors. LiveLaw names Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, the Delhi Police Commissioner and the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation. Counter-affidavits and a compliance report are due on 13 Oct. Personal appearance is dispensed with for now. Notice was also issued on the habeas corpus petition. Menaka Guruswamy argued that it covers the illegal detention of about 7,000 people, not only named leaders. The order says lawyers, journalists and other professionals shall not be hindered in any manner whatsoever. Metro and trains are to run normally, subject to Article 19(2). People may move freely, and barricades are to be reviewed forthwith. The internet is not to be hindered. There is to be no illegal detention of peaceful unarmed assemblies beyond the Section 163 BNSS area, and the Section 163 board at the court is to come down. The case is listed again on 13 Oct with the other tagged petitions. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta denied any violation. He said 45 of 303 Metro stations were closed for law and order, denied that anyone was illegally detained, and called the habeas plea infructuous because detainees had been released. That is his submission, as recorded in the order.

The Supreme Court special bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana passed its interim order. The court rose about 12:36 PM. Bar & Bench (12:51 PM): no illegal detention except by procedure established by law; Metro and trains to run normally unless regulation is needed for public order; free movement, subject to traffic rules, with barricades to be reviewed forthwith; the internet shall remain undisturbed, as per law; peaceful assembly is allowed, particularly outside the Section 163 BNSS zone; the Section 163 notice board near the Supreme Court is to come down. The court recorded an assurance that lawyers, journalists and other professionals will not be obstructed. A contempt notice was issued. A short affidavit to show cause, and a compliance report including Metro restrictions and railway advisories, are due Tuesday 13 Oct, when the habeas pleas and connected matters will also be heard. The principal contempt petition is advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi's, against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chair D. Thara. This is the written order. It replaces the earlier report that the order was still being dictated and that the full text was awaited. The signed order, uploaded at about 5:25 PM, finds a prima facie case of contempt. See that update.

Justice Joymalya Bagchi, wrapping up at about 1:59 PM (The Hindu, Krishnadas Rajagopal): "We have issued notices on all the petitions. Union government would file its counter affidavit. We have sought from the Union government the reasons and circumstances behind the prohibitory orders under S. 163 BNSS. We have sought the Union government's response to petitions alleging police assault on people, particularly protesters, lawyers and journalists. As far as the Delhi Union of Journalists' petition on seizure of journalists' devices, the SG has said there were no such seizures. We have asked him to make good this statement in the counter affidavit." The assault allegations are the petitioners' claims. The Solicitor General's denial of device seizures is his statement, still to be put in the counter. Earlier in the hearing he had said, on who counts as a journalist, "In our experience, any person having a mobile phone is a journalist" (Indian Express). The Chief Justice said, "Everybody acting as journalists will create problems," and that the harassment instances cited by the Network of Women in Media, India, should be investigated (The Hindu, 1:33 PM). Senior advocate Indira Jaising, for NWMI, said police cannot investigate themselves and sought a committee. The Hindu: the Chief Justice prima facie agreed to a committee whose members and chairperson are all women, and asked Ms Jaising to suggest names in a sealed cover. She had also referred to a woman judge as chair, in line with the Vishaka guidelines. The court said no coercive action should be taken against the woman journalist booked by Delhi Police after she alleged harassment. The Hindu describes that case as a booking following allegations that she publicly humiliated officers and used casteist slurs. Jaising's account, as Indian Express reported it, is that she was booked under the SC/ST Atrocities Act after accusing an assistant commissioner of sexual harassment, and that her own complaint was not registered. Both descriptions are kept. Justice Bagchi said the court will examine whether freedom of expression means every citizen can claim to be a journalist. The Hindu (1:08 PM): notice also on Bhanu Sanoriya's plea, argued by senior advocate A.N.S. Nadkarni, that protest organisers take personal responsibility for harm to others. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan said that prayer cuts both ways and that the police must also be accountable. Indian Express reported the same exchange with the Solicitor General, including responsibility for the Police Commissioner. The court also agreed to hear street vendors' compensation pleas. A lawyer told the court vendors had not earned even Rs 500 over Dussehra and Diwali. That is the lawyer's claim.

The Indian Youth Congress marched from Patel Chowk metro along Ashoka Road and was stopped near Parliament Street police station. Protesters were detained. Police cited BNSS Sec 163. The number detained was not released by police. Traffic was disrupted in the New Delhi district.

LiveLaw (6:08 PM): Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice on three prayers in the Indian Youth Congress plea, (c), (d) and (f), and listed the matter for 17 Nov. Prayer (c) seeks a declaration that the 2022 standing order cannot automatically prohibit a peaceful assembly. Prayer (d) seeks a fresh, reasoned reconsideration of the protest request. Prayer (f) seeks a declaration that the 10-day notice rule is not an absolute bar. Senior advocate Siddharth Luthra, for president Uday Bhanu Chib, said he would amend the prayers after Monday's de-notification and called conditions in the 2022 order "Completely non speaking" and "bad in law." Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma opposed notice. He said the petition is about holding a demonstration at Jantar Mantar, that the site was de-notified pursuant to Supreme Court orders, and that the petition cannot stand unless the de-notification is challenged. Notice on those three prayers is not an order granting permission to protest, and it is not a ruling on the de-notification itself.

India Today (published 8:04 PM, updated 8:29 PM), Bar & Bench (about 8:20 PM) and NDTV published the petition's ten prayers. In paraphrase of that prayer block: (1) the Election Commission to produce the complete files, agendas, minutes, notings and objections of the Election Commissioners on disputed SIR decisions, plus ECINET and ERONET access logs and the complete file for the 24 June 2025 decision to begin nationwide SIR; (2) examine whether those decisions complied with Article 324, Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, and T.N. Seshan v. Union of India, and quash and set aside any decision taken without lawful authority; (3) action against persons responsible for breaches, including under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, where warranted; (4) pending adjudication, every SIR-related Commission decision to be taken and minuted under Section 18; (5) online Form 6 to conform to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, unless those Rules are lawfully amended; (6) an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, with technical experts, to audit SIR deletions and database access, including ECINET and ERONET, and to review EVM policies, procedures and technical design against global best practices; (7) booth-wise publication of deleted electors with reasons and a gender and age breakdown, and a working way to restore eligible names; (8) no deletion without notice and a hearing, and eligible persons in Punjab and other poll-bound States allowed to seek inclusion until the last date the law allows; (9) an interim direction suspending the ongoing SIR across States pending adjudication; (10) other orders the court finds fit. The published prayer block does not ask for the Chief Election Commissioner's removal. India Today's introduction describes the plea as challenging the validity of SIR. The petition text in the same story says it does not seek to reopen the validity of SIR after the court's 27 May 2026 judgment in ADR v ECI. It challenges implementation and whether the Commission acted as a collective institution. The petition cites an Indian Express report of 23 September 2026 that the two Election Commissioners had recorded objections. It notes that the Commission says differences are normal and that decisions were unanimous. Both accounts are kept.

Very important12 Oct, 1:29 PMIST

The Keralam Legislative Assembly passed a resolution seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar (The Hindu, updated 2:14 PM; Hindustan Times; ThePrint). Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan moved it. The House took it up from about 12:52 PM and it had passed by about 1:29 PM. UDF and LDF supported it. The BJP objected and proposed amendments that were rejected. The resolution seeks Kumar's removal, steps to improve the Election Commission's transparency, action by the Centre and the Commission on defects in the Special Intensive Revision, restoration of voting rights to eligible voters wrongly excluded, and a selection panel that again includes the Chief Justice of India alongside the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition, citing an earlier Supreme Court order. Satheesan accepted Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan's amendment changing "lakhs" of excluded voters to "crores". A state Assembly resolution is not binding. Under Article 324(5) a Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge, by a special-majority motion in Parliament. Separately, PTI (about 2:49 PM) reported Satheesan denying political vendetta in a Vigilance probe into allegations linked to a road project involving Kumar when he was Kerala PWD secretary: "It is not political. There is no political vendetta." His words.

In September last year the then LDF government passed a resolution against rolling out the Special Intensive Revision. Times of India, the Economic Times and Indian Express: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan is to move it under Rule 118 on the opening day of the Assembly's second session. Besides removal of the Chief Election Commissioner, it seeks reinstatement of eligible voters struck off during the Special Intensive Revision and changes to the selection panel for Election Commissioners, including restoring the Chief Justice of India, per India Today. The Economic Times says the opposition LDF has decided to back it, so passage is expected, and gives the House as UDF 102, LDF 35 and BJP 3 in a 140-member Assembly. The Economic Times notes a state Assembly resolution is not binding. Under Article 324(5) a Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge, by a special-majority motion in Parliament. It was not reported as passed as of 12:10 PM. Update, about 12:52–1:29 PM: The Hindu (updated 2:14 PM), Hindustan Times and ThePrint report that the Keralam Legislative Assembly passed the resolution. UDF and LDF supported it. The BJP objected and proposed amendments that were rejected. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan accepted Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan's amendment changing "lakhs" of excluded voters to "crores". The resolution also seeks steps to improve the Election Commission's transparency and a selection panel that includes the Chief Justice of India alongside the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition, citing an earlier Supreme Court order. A state Assembly resolution is still not binding. Under Article 324(5) a Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge, by a special-majority motion in Parliament. Separately, PTI (about 2:49 PM) reported Satheesan denying political vendetta in a Vigilance probe into allegations linked to a road project involving Gyanesh Kumar when he was Kerala PWD secretary: "It is not political. There is no political vendetta." His words.

The Bombay High Court (Goa bench) ordered the release of CJP activists detained at Azad Maidan in Panaji. Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar held a special Sunday-evening hearing on habeas corpus pleas by Melisa Simoes and Rui Gomes Pereira. Senior Advocate Norma Alvares appeared with Om D'Costa. Alvares, via PTI, said the hearing ran from about 7:30 PM to 8:45 PM. Times of India quotes the court: "Considering that there are no prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, we are of the opinion that the detention may not have been authorised." The bench was told an executive magistrate gave oral instructions to detain them because they "barged into" Azad Maidan. The court did not rule on whether the detention was correct. The public prosecutor assured the court they would be released. Alvares gave an undertaking that they would not protest at Azad Maidan on Sunday night only. The Goan: they were released around 9:40 PM from Panaji police station after a bus brought them back from Pernem police station. Times of India and The Goan name seven: Jack Sukhija, Amreen Shaikh (Times of India spells the name Afreen), Aditya Parulekar, Bhupesh Bind, Liston Noronha, Shamiro or Shamino Fernandes, and Milind Rane. PTI and India Today say six. Both counts are kept. The court ordered the Panaji and Pernem station in-charges to file affidavits on the reasons for the detention and on why the peaceful protest was not allowed. Further hearing Monday 12 Oct at noon (The Goan). A medical exam at Goa Medical College was offered because two were reportedly injured (Alvares). Alvares also argued that Shaikh, a woman, could not be detained after 6 PM (Times of India). Jack Sukhija, after release, told PTI that phones were taken away and they were not allowed to contact anyone. His claim. This confirms the 9:09 PM post by TOI journalist Bindiya Chari. PTI reported it at 11:22 PM, India Today at 10:50 PM, and New Indian Express at 11:16 PM.

Under the constitutional scheme the court cannot take cognisance of such grievances on the administrative side. The court has judicial review powers under Article 32, and if a petition is filed on Monday it will be taken up the following day, Tuesday 13 Oct, when the already pending matters are listed. The court is committed to fundamental rights and its doors are always open. The march is still set for 1:30 PM from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba Road junction to the Supreme Court, about 2 km.

The Supreme Court's written order is out. LiveLaw and Bar & Bench: the court finds a prima facie case of contempt over the Metro and train shutdown, treated as a violation of its 9 Oct order. Notice went to the alleged contemnors. LiveLaw names Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, the Delhi Police Commissioner and the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation. Counter-affidavits and a compliance report are due on 13 Oct. Personal appearance is dispensed with for now. Notice was also issued on the habeas corpus petition. Menaka Guruswamy argued that it covers the illegal detention of about 7,000 people, not only named leaders. The order says lawyers, journalists and other professionals shall not be hindered in any manner whatsoever. Metro and trains are to run normally, subject to Article 19(2). People may move freely, and barricades are to be reviewed forthwith. The internet is not to be hindered. There is to be no illegal detention of peaceful unarmed assemblies beyond the Section 163 BNSS area, and the Section 163 board at the court is to come down. The case is listed again on 13 Oct with the other tagged petitions. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta denied any violation. He said 45 of 303 Metro stations were closed for law and order, denied that anyone was illegally detained, and called the habeas plea infructuous because detainees had been released. That is his submission, as recorded in the order.

The principal contempt petition is advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi's, against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chair D. Thara. This is the written order. It replaces the earlier report that the order was still being dictated and that the full text was awaited. The signed order, uploaded at about 5:25 PM, finds a prima facie case of contempt. See that update.

Gopal Sankaranarayanan handed over video stills of action against lawyers, including Shadan Farasat, and flagged the Section 163 order outside the court.

Background

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth movement, along with Left groups, student unions and civil-society groups, called a protest at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi, on Sat 10 Oct 2026. They want Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls scrapped. Critics say SIR has removed more than 130 million names (NPR/AP). Delhi Police refused permission and locked down central Delhi: BNSS Sec 163 orders, about 45 metro stations shut until gates reopened around 10:36 PM, trains cancelled, internet cut within 4 km, and roughly 23,000 CAPF personnel deployed. Police detained CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on board their flight. YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained at his Gurugram home. Opposition leaders, lawyers and journalists were also detained. INDIA bloc street protests have been running since about 2 Oct, and Rahul Gandhi was detained on 6 and 7 Oct. As of 9:15 PM on 13 Oct 2026, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde were still held. No release was reported. ANI (about 8:44–8:47 PM) said Delhi Police registered a case against Das, Ranka and others for "unauthorised trespassing through the house" over entering Jantar Mantar today. No penal section was confirmed by a reliable outlet. An account @CJP_for_India, which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, posted at about 7:27 PM that the leaders had not yet been released. That post is unverified. Amit Shah cited BJP wins in Rajasthan local-body polls held on ballot papers as an answer to EVM claims, asked Rahul Gandhi to introspect, and said people know Gandhi's plans of getting infiltrators registered as voters. Those are Shah's claims. Pawan Khera said Shah's statement proved the opposition's allegations. His claim. Congress MP Varsha Gaikwad said INDIA bloc parties will join district- and block-level protests on 14 Oct. PTI reported the bloc vowing to keep resisting what it calls vote theft and to reclaim Jantar Mantar. At the evening press conference Rahul Gandhi said the net is closing around Narendra Modi, Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar, and that the next step is a surprise. The Hindu reported journalists at the Press Club of India condemning the police crackdown on the media on 10 and 11 Oct. The Indian Youth Congress asked for an independent, time-bound inquiry into police action during the protests. The Supreme Court protest cluster is listed for Thursday 15 Oct. Rahul Gandhi's Special Intensive Revision petition is also on that day's cause list, before Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi (PTI via Deccan Herald, 7:27 PM on 14 Oct; The Hindu; Business Today). The Hindu says Justice V. Mohana is not sitting on 15 Oct and that the regular three-judge bench stands cancelled. Indian Express (6:47 AM on 15 Oct) says the batch of petitions on the 10 Oct protest clampdown and transport shutdown is to be heard along with the Gandhi plea. Moneycontrol (11:08 PM on 14 Oct) reported the plea was unlikely to be heard on 15 Oct. Both expectations are kept. No outcome was reported as of 9:00 AM. As of 9:00 AM IST on Thu 15 Oct 2026, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are in Tihar Jail on five days' judicial custody from 14 Oct. Police cite repeated violations and a breach of the peace bond. Abhijeet Dipke says they were jailed only for unfurling the Tricolour. His words. The CJP legal team has sought bail at Patiala House. No bail order was reported. Ajinkya Shinde was released on 14 Oct on a personal bond of Rs 5,000. Indian Express says the condition lasts one year. ABP Live says six months. Both accounts are kept. Dipke said 11 other CJP activists detained with them were released. His post. He has called a Tricolour gathering at Central Park, Connaught Place, on Friday 16 Oct at 5 PM. Hindustan Times (7:47 AM) reported that Delhi Police are planning security for that call and that officers said no mass gathering should be allowed in central Delhi, including Connaught Place. No permission for that gathering was reported as of 9:00 AM. Times of India (published 7:05 AM) says the Special Executive Magistrate matter is listed for further inquiry on 19 Oct. On Thu 15 Oct a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi held an hour-long hearing on the batch of protest, SIR and denotification petitions (Indian Express). The court issued notice on Rahul Gandhi's INDIA-bloc SIR petition to the Election Commission of India, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, named as a personal respondent, and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi (LiveLaw; NDTV). LiveLaw also reported notice on Asaduddin Owaisi's SIR plea. The Hindu's 12:59 PM live entry referred to the Digvijaya Singh and Owaisi petitions as well. Indian Express reported notice to the Election Commission on a Form 6 modification plea. No interim stay or suspension of SIR was reported. LiveLaw said similar SIR matters are listed for Tuesday. The Chief Justice said issuing notice does not condone the conduct, and that one petitioner must explain his conduct. Indian Express quoted the bench: "We have no problem with the other petitioners… We are issuing notice, but we are not condoning the conduct." NDTV quoted him: "We will issue notice but we want to know his conduct on the next date of hearing." The Hindu (12:59 PM) reported notice on a criminal-contempt petition by Digant Mishra, argued by senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia, over Rahul Gandhi leading a procession into the Supreme Court. NDTV reported notice to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and others on a separate plea against that march, and an order to preserve CCTV from the court premises. The Chief Justice said, "Nobody can browbeat the judiciary," and called the attempts "feeble" (NDTV; The Hindu). Indian Express reported that police were told to preserve all CCTV of the protests. Notice also went on the challenge to de-notification of Jantar Mantar. The Hindu names the petitioner as Swaty Singh. Indian Express names Swaty Malik, represented by senior advocate Mukta Gupta, and says the Union and the Delhi Police Commissioner were asked to reply. NDTV Profit reported Solicitor General Tushar Mehta saying a committee had been constituted before the decision. Indian Express: Justice Bagchi said the court must examine whether oral observations can be construed as law, because the government affidavit had tied the move to the 9 Oct order, and that "heard" must also be understood from the perspective of technology. Sites already named by police are Burari Ground, Ramlila Maidan or Ramlila Ground, and CBD Ground. On the contempt affidavits, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan and Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar used "unconditional and unqualified apology" language while defending the 10 Oct steps (Indian Express; LiveLaw). The Hindu (12:57 PM): the Solicitor General said the media misread the opening apology, which is the usual form in a contempt reply, and that the affidavits go on to defend the measures. NDTV Profit reported that the court treated an apology accompanied by justification as a qualified one. At about 6:07 PM the Home Ministry, via PIB, said that opening is mandatory whenever a contempt notice is answered (The Hindu). Mohan said cellular internet was suspended from 10 PM on 9 Oct to 10 PM on 10 Oct only within 4 km of Raisina Hill, and that Wi-Fi and broadband were not suspended (LiveLaw; Indian Express). The Delhi High Court, Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma, refused to restrain CJP and Abhijeet Dipke from the 16 Oct Central Park gathering. It did not grant express permission. It recorded Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma's assurance that police had taken steps to control CJP's activities and would address the petitioner's concerns. When counsel pressed for a specific restrain order, the bench said, "Don't insist. We have passed the order." Further consideration is on 3 Nov 2026 (India Today; The Hindu). NDMC said Central Park, Connaught Place, will stay closed to the general public on 16 and 17 Oct for "administrative reasons" (PTI via The Hindu, 7:37 PM; ThePrint). At about 8:35 PM a senior officer said Connaught Place is not a designated protest site, and that protesters can use Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground or CBD Ground after permission, with paramilitary companies, barricades and traffic regulation already in place (The Hindu / PTI). At about 8:38 PM Delhi Police urged people to stay away from CJP's Lehra Do Tiranga march but said it could facilitate a select group to wave the national flag and sing the national anthem at a suitable place, citing BNSS Sec 163 already in force in Connaught Place and adjoining areas (The Hindu / PTI). At the Press Club, CJP restated three demands: the CEC's resignation over alleged SIR irregularities, release of Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and all detained peaceful protesters, and an end to police brutality with Jantar Mantar restored as a protest site (The Hindu, 5:42 PM). Dipke, Prashant Bhushan and Prakash Raj made further claims, recorded below as their words. As of 9:00 PM, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka remain in Tihar on five days' judicial custody from 14 Oct. No bail order, grant or rejection was reported. The Special Executive Magistrate inquiry is still listed for 19 Oct (Times of India). Ajinkya Shinde remains released on a personal bond.

Key people detained

Status chip, then the recorded time and place.

Dhruv Rathee

Very importantReleased

YouTuber; flew in from Germany, joined CJP's Bengaluru protest on 8 Oct

Time 10 Oct, about 7:48 AM IST (police entered the flat, per The Hindu); CJP said about 8 AM

Place His parents' flat, Sector 56, Gurugram. The Hindu names the society as Central Park Vihar; HT names it Kendriya Vihar. Joint Delhi and Gurugram Police operation

RELEASED (~3 AM, 11 Oct). ThePrint (2:18 PM): "I did not sign any bond, I did not sign any undertaking, I did not sign any condition for release." His words. Hindustan Times (11:47 AM) reports his Instagram caption: "I was not arrested or detained, I was KIDNAPPED." HT says he gave no undertaking to Gurugram Police. His claim. The Hindu (10:53 AM) says the Gurugram Crime Branch released him around 2 AM. HT and PTI, citing officials, say about 3 AM. Both times are kept. HT's 11:47 AM story says he was detained around 9:30 AM on Saturday. HT's earlier story said about 7:30 AM. Both accounts are kept. Hindustan Times, citing officials, says Dhruv Rathee was released at 3 AM on Sunday and handed over to his family. He had been picked up from his residence in Kendriya Vihar society, Gurugram Sector 56, around 7:30 AM on Saturday. An unnamed police officer, quoted by PTI, said: "He can be detained again, or further legal action might be taken if he tries to go to Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders." This corrects earlier reports that he was still in custody, including ETV Bharat (6:48 AM) and ET Now (~7:19 AM). Earlier account: Taken to an undisclosed place in Gurugram. No release reported NDTV (~10 PM) says he remained in custody, with Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Delhi Police sources (ANI, 9:38 PM) said detainees other than CJP leaders had been released. No outlet has reported a release as of 11:10 PM. NDTV (~10 PM) still has him in custody. Social claims of a release are unverified and contradicted by NDTV. Arvind Kejriwal (his own post, 10:03 PM) asked the Prime Minister where Dipke, Ranka, Rathee and Das are being held. HT (11:25 PM) says he is still held, with Dipke, Das and Ranka, while everyone else was released. NDTV says he remained in custody as of 12:15 AM. Social posts claiming he is out are unverified and contradicted by NDTV. LawBeat says a Supreme Court habeas plea also names him; Bar & Bench's report does not mention him (single source). That plea was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. CJP says it did not file or approve it, and Bharti has sought to withdraw it. On 12 Oct, India Today (updated 12:16 PM), reporting what he told The Lallantop: he wants to join the INDIA bloc march but alleges about 50 police outside his residence, three or four cars following him, and threats that he would be picked up again if he went near a protest. Asked if this was house arrest, he said: "Unofficially, I would say so." His claim. No police confirmation was found as of 9:35 PM. He also said: "I am an Indian citizen, there is no visa issue for me." His words. This does not change the Sunday release. On 14 Oct, a Delhi court issued fresh summons to him in the 2018 defamation case over his "BJP IT Cell" video. The next hearing is 17 Oct (NDTV; New Indian Express, 14 Oct). That case is separate from the protest case. ThePrint: he claims Delhi Police are following him in unmarked cars. His claim. No police confirmation was found.

Police (via HT) say he refused requests not to travel to Delhi for a protest that had no permission

Abhijeet Dipke

Very importantReleased

CJP founder

Time 10 Oct, about 10:30 AM IST (ThePrint live blog)

Place On board an Air India flight from Mumbai, just after landing at IGI Airport, Delhi. Later moved to Gurugram (TOI)

RELEASED (~10 AM, 11 Oct). On X at 4:26 PM he wrote, "Haven't signed any bond that says we won't protest. We will hit the streets again." That is his statement (Indian Express, 5:11 PM). Separately, LiveLaw (10:20 AM), citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh, says the magistrate released him, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on condition they would not breach the peace for one year. PTI (10:54 AM) says they must "maintain peace" for one year. Delhi Police, via ANI (10:56 AM), say a surety of Rs 50,000 was taken for peace and good behaviour for one year. CJP says that bond only bars a breach of the peace, and that peaceful protest is a constitutional right. Both accounts are kept. He said CJP will hit the streets again. NDTV (5:56 PM): CJP vowed protests across the country. Delhi Police, at a press conference around 5:29 PM, released a video of officers telling him of his grandmother's death. DCP Neha Yadav (ANI, 5:38 PM) said officers offered all possible assistance, including flights and phone calls, and repeatedly asked if he wished to speak to his parents, but he declined. Hindustan Times says the clip shows him declining an offer to return home. That is the police account. CJP's Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das say he was denied permission to speak to his cousin, and they accuse the police of insensitivity. That is CJP's account. Both are kept. Hindustan Times names his grandmother as Savitribai Dipke and says she died on Saturday at the family home in Santuk Pimpri, and that he left for the village on Sunday. The Tribune, with PTI, reports that the last rites were held on Sunday morning and that he missed them. His uncle Vilas Dipke said he pleaded with Delhi Police at least 10 times to release him, and that the release came too late for the funeral. The family says he will be present to collect her ashes. Delhi Police deny any delay. They say he was informed and offered help to travel, and that he declined. Both accounts are kept. He flew to Nagpur and spoke there before going on to Hingoli (Tribune, 7:17 PM; PTI, 6:33 PM): "We will hit the streets again. We are not afraid of PM Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah ... Put me in jail a hundred times." His words. On X at 6:31 PM he said he had asked for his phone for a couple of minutes to get his cousin's number, and had asked to speak to a lawyer, and that both were refused. At 7:24 PM he wrote, "Why did you delete the part where I was asking for my phone ... and where I was asking to let me speak to my lawyers?" He accuses police of editing the clip. His claim. State Mirror, quoting him via Neha Bora's team account, says that at 3:30 AM police told him to call his father and say he was going to jail for a long time. That is his account. PTI (7:52 PM) describes the police video: a woman officer offered transport, and he repeatedly said "I'll stay." An Executive Magistrate ordered the release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:58 AM, citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench, 10:00 AM, which reports them released). This corrects earlier reports, including this page's 8:15 AM update, that they were still in custody. LiveLaw (10:20 AM), citing Ratna Singh, says they were released on condition they will not engage in a breach of the peace for one year. PTI (10:54 AM) says the condition is that they "maintain peace" for one year. Delhi Police, via ANI (10:56 AM), say the preventive arrest was under BNSS Sections 126 and 170 on 10 Oct 2026, that all due legal procedures were followed, that they were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate's court at Delhi Cantt, and that a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was taken. That is the police account. CJP counsel Soutik Banerjee said at 10:18 AM that all three had been released (LiveLaw). Indian Express (10:51 AM) says they walked out of Delhi Cantt police station. Delhi Police had placed the three under preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 (security for keeping the peace) and 170 (arrest to prevent the commission of cognisable offences) (LiveLaw, 8:23 AM; Bar & Bench, 8:32 AM; PTI, 9:10 AM; Indian Express, 9:34 AM). They were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate, South West District, at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:35 AM; Bar & Bench, 9:39 AM; ANI video, 9:51 AM). India Today (9:00 AM, police sources) had said that no arrests had been made. His mother, Anita Dipke, said he was not allowed to attend his grandmother's funeral (PTI video, 11:12 AM). PTI (12:40 PM) and Indian Express (1:02 PM): his paternal grandmother, Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke, 85, died on Saturday in Hingoli district, Maharashtra, after a prolonged illness, and the last rites were performed on Sunday morning. He missed them. The family says Delhi Police did not release him in time despite repeated pleas. Delhi Police said he was informed and offered help to travel home; his uncle Vilas Dipke disputed that. PTI video (12:46 PM), as he left Kapil Sibal's residence: "I am going home now to be with my family, as my grandmother has passed away. Ashutosh and Saurav will hold a press conference at 2 pm and announce the future course of action... The entire Delhi was brought to a standstill to protect Gyanesh Kumar." His words. Hindustan Times (1:28 PM) says he is heading back to his village and that he says CJP will not back down. The Wire (12:57 PM) quotes him: "October 10 will go down as the beginning of the end of this dictatorship." His words. He was in Delhi until about 10 AM. After release he wrote, as reported by Hindustan Times and The Wire: "Modi, as PM, is an embarrassment to India. Never has this country seen a bigger coward and bully." His words. Hindustan Times says the three were held from inside the plane: flight AI 2428 landed at 10:18 AM on Saturday and was moved to remote bay R12 (people aware of the matter, per HT). Earlier account: CJP alleges he has no access to lawyers. His grandmother died in Hingoli the same day Police sources (PTI, ~4:06 PM) say he was told of his grandmother's death and left to decide whether to stay or go home for her last rites. Delhi Police (via ANI, ~4:26 PM) say he was offered help to travel home on humanitarian grounds for his grandmother's funeral. At 1:08 PM, intelligence sources told The Hindu that Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to three different locations in Delhi-NCR. CJP said at ~4:45 PM it still has no information on Dipke, Das and Ranka's whereabouts and is concerned for their safety. 5:20 PM: CJP publicly appealed to Delhi Police to release Dipke immediately, saying his whereabouts are still unknown, his lawyers cannot reach him and his family cannot tell him of his grandmother's death (CJP claim). This conflicts with police sources earlier saying he was informed; both accounts are kept, attributed. Delhi Police (via IANS, 7:12 PM) say Dipke's grandmother's death was promptly conveyed to him with due sensitivity, he was told the funeral time, and he was offered all possible assistance to travel home. NDTV (7:41 PM) says that by evening it was not clear whether he would be released. CJP said at a 7:35 PM press conference it still has no information on the whereabouts of Dipke, Das and Ranka (The Hindu). Police sources (The Hindu, 7:38 PM) say due legal process will be followed in the case of CJP leaders. Ajinkya Shinde (CJP, ~8:55 PM) alleges police did not let Dipke speak to his lawyer or family after news of his grandmother's death. CJP says Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to different locations across Delhi-NCR (The Hindu; IANS, 9:04 PM). SFI joint secretary Aishe Ghosh demanded their release (The Hindu, 8:35 PM). NDTV (~10 PM) says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remained in custody. Delhi Police sources (ANI, 9:38 PM): all detainees were released from detention centres except CJP leaders, and due legal process will be followed for the CJP leaders. 10:47 PM: Hindustan Times reports Delhi Police posted on X that Dipke was "immediately" told of his grandmother's death and the funeral time and was offered "possible facilitation" to travel home; CJP replied, "Where is Abhijeet? His family wants to talk to him... last rites tomorrow morning." 10:53 PM: CJP posted, "It's been 12 hours. No information. No accountability," and demanded immediate release, disclosure of whereabouts and access to lawyers for Dipke, Das and Ranka. NDTV says police told Dipke he could leave for his grandmother's funeral, but it is unclear whether he will be released. Nothing new was reported on that beyond the earlier police and CJP accounts. HT (11:25 PM) says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee are still held while everyone else was released. NDTV says the four remained in custody as of 12:15 AM, and that everyone else among at least 3,000 detainees was released. Ajinkya Shinde wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner at 11:29 PM asking where Dipke, Das and Ranka are (IANS). A habeas corpus plea seeking their production and release was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. CJP legal cell chief Ratna Singh posted at 12:48 AM: "This petition is not filed by @Cockroachisback. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." CJP reposted that and added "Please note." Bar & Bench and LiveLaw report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. Ratna Singh posted at 1:03 AM: "Since morning no one knows where they are, their families don't have any idea, the lawyers have no clue." Says he signed no bond (Tribune, updated 9:57 PM); that conflicts with Ratna Singh's earlier account of a one-year no-breach-of-peace condition. Both are kept. India Today (9:16 PM): he questioned an alleged 3:30 AM call in which officers asked him to tell his parents he could be jailed "for a long time." His account. ThePrint (8:47 PM): he rejected the police claim that they offered help, saying they "wanted to torment my parents." His words. DCP Neha Yadav (Indian Express, 9:19 PM) shared the police video and said permission for the protest was denied because of past non-compliance. That is the police account. IANS (10:31 PM and 11:07 PM), ANI (12:11 AM) and PTI video (12:13 AM): he reached his ancestral village, Santuk Pimpri in Hingoli, late on Sunday night and visited the cremation ground to pay tribute to his grandmother. NDTV (11:07 PM) carries the police video of officers telling him of her death, headlined "We're Sorry." On 12 Oct in Hingoli (PTI video, 10:16 AM; IANS, 10:29–10:32 AM) he said: "Delhi Police, if you have the courage, release the entire video in which I repeatedly asked them to let me speak to my cousin, give me my phone for two minutes and allow me to speak to my lawyer." He also said police may have felt ashamed of alleged molestation by male officers and so used female officers. That is his allegation. On X, via PTI and The Hindu (11:13 AM): "Youth are being assaulted, journalists are being assaulted, even MPs are being assaulted by Delhi Police. What makes Gyanesh Kumar so indispensable to Modi that he is willing to wage war against everyone just to protect him?" His words. The police account remains that he was offered help and declined. On 12 Oct he wrote on X (about 1:46 PM): "They have removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Yes, it's no a longer protest site as anyway it was turned into a war zone by the coward dictator. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!" About 1:59 PM: "Today, Modi denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Tomorrow, he will denotify democracy itself. The dictator's problem was never the protest site. It was the very idea of people protesting." His words. PTI (about 2:24 PM), from Hingoli, reported his allegation that Delhi Police subjected him and his family to "mental torture" and that his relatives and lawyer were unaware of his whereabouts during the 10 Oct detention. His allegation. The police account already on this card is that officers told him of his grandmother's death and offered help. On X at about 5:04 PM on 12 Oct he wrote: "If Modi thinks taking away Jantar Mantar will put an end to protests, he is mistaken. Jantar Mantar is not just a location but a spirit of resistance..." His words. As of 6:15 PM, the 24-hour ultimatum given at Parliament Street around 11:50 AM still had no police response in the reports used here. As of 9:35 PM IST, that 24-hour ultimatum still had no reported police grant of a Jantar Mantar date. On 13 Oct he posted that CJP members carrying the tricolour had entered Jantar Mantar early in the morning before police picked them up, and wrote, tagging the Prime Minister: "You cannot denotify the resistance." His claim (The Hindu / PTI). He was not reported detained in these accounts. Das, Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde were. ETV Bharat (about 3:08 PM, 13 Oct) reported his claim that Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and Saurav Das were held at separate locations, that 11 volunteers were taken elsewhere, and that lawyers were barred and threatened with further detention. He asked, "How can you arrest someone for hoisting the tricolour?" His claim. He was not reported detained. The Hindu and PTI (about 4:31 PM): he was in his village, Santuk Pimpri, in Maharashtra's Hingoli district, for the asthi visarjan of his grandmother, Savitribai Dipke. He warned that if demonstrations are banned at Jantar Mantar, protest sites would emerge across the country. He said that if police stop him on the way to Delhi he would begin the agitation from wherever he is detained, and that he would reach the capital on Wednesday. His words. He was not reported detained. Times of India (about 5:52 PM), citing ANI, reported a later post and interview in which he said Saurav, Ashutosh and Ajinkya were still detained and that police were not letting lawyers meet them. He called it kidnapping. He said Ratna Singh had just told him the three were kept separately. His account. PTI (about 8:49 PM): his father, in Hingoli, said the BJP and the RSS have taken over institutions and that his son is protecting democracy. That is the father's claim. Dipke was not reported detained. 15 Oct, Press Club of India, afternoon: he was not reported detained. With AISA's Neha Bora, senior advocate Prashant Bhushan, actor-activist Prakash Raj and SFI's Aishe Ghosh, he addressed the press (The Hindu; photo credit Shashi Shekhar Kashyap). The Hindu live (7:13 PM) headlined that chaos erupted at the Dipke–Neha Bora press conference. CJP restated three demands: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged SIR irregularities; release of Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and all detained peaceful protesters; and an end to police brutality, with Jantar Mantar restored as a designated protest site (The Hindu, 5:42 PM). Those are CJP's demands. Dipke asked: "Why is Gyanesh Kumar so important to Narendra Modi? Why should we not believe that Gyanesh Kumar is helping Narendra Modi win elections?" (PTI via The Hindu, 6:13 PM). At 3:40 PM he said: "You have called unfurling the Tricolour a violation of law. For whom? For Gyanesh Kumar?" His words (PTI via The Hindu). The Delhi High Court later refused to restrain him and CJP from the Friday Central Park call and did not grant express permission. It recorded Delhi Police's assurance that the gathering would be regulated (India Today; The Hindu, about 4:44–5:36 PM). NDMC then said Central Park will be closed to the public on 16 and 17 Oct for administrative reasons (PTI via The Hindu, 7:37 PM). At about 8:38 PM Delhi Police urged people to stay away from the Lehra Do Tiranga march but said a select group could wave the flag and sing the anthem at a suitable place under BNSS Sec 163 (The Hindu / PTI). Both the CJP call and the police regulation are kept.

Protest was banned / had no permission. No written grounds reported

Saurav Das

Very importantUnknown

CJP leader / co-convener

Time 10 Oct, about 10:30 AM IST

Place Same flight, IGI Airport. Later moved to another location in Delhi (TOI)

JAILED — 5 days' judicial custody (Tihar), from 14 Oct. On the morning of 14 Oct, Delhi Police placed him, with the others named here, under preventive arrest and produced them before the Special Executive Magistrate court at Mandir Marg. Das and Ranka were remanded to five days' judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail (Indian Express; The Hindu, updated 12:16 AM on 15 Oct; BBC, about 9:55 AM on 14 Oct; AP). Delhi Police, via Indian Express: "In view of their alleged repeated attempts to disturb public peace and violate the law, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ajinkya Shinde were arrested under the relevant preventive provisions of law. Their alleged attempts to instigate others through social media to engage in similar unlawful activities were also taken into consideration." Police said custody was "for repeated violations of law and serious apprehension that if released on bail, they will again violate the law and instigate others." That is the police account. Times of India (published 7:05 AM, 15 Oct) headlined that the court said if released on bail "they will violate law, instigate others." The same report says the matter is listed for further inquiry on 19 Oct. Indian Express, on the 13 Oct entry: a group of 14 allegedly used a lane to reach the JD(U) office premises and climbed its locked iron gate to enter Jantar Mantar, unfurled the Tricolour and raised slogans, and were taken to a police station about 40 km away. CJP says phones were taken. India Today (video, published 1:07 PM on 14 Oct): the CJP legal team is moving Patiala House Court for bail for Das and Ranka, arguing that BNSS procedure was violated during the SEM inquiry, and that the SEM relied on conduct and social media posts. He remains in Tihar on the five days' judicial custody from 14 Oct. Times of India says the Special Executive Magistrate matter is still listed for further inquiry on 19 Oct. The Patiala House bail application reported on 14 Oct (India Today) had no grant or rejection in the reports checked today. India Today says he is in Tihar Jail No. 2, as an undertrial after medical checks. Earlier account: Held. Detained again on the morning of 13 Oct at Jantar Mantar, with Ajinkya Shinde (The Hindu, the Economic Times and Times of India; reports from about 9:48 AM). No release was reported as of 12:15 PM. From a detention bus he said: "Jantar Mantar has been breached. We were inside and now they are detaining us and taking us away" (Times of India). The Hindu (about 11:13 AM) reported him saying they had been taken to Jaffarpur police station. Abhijeet Dipke posted that they had entered with the tricolour before police picked them up. His claim. A senior Delhi Police officer told The Hindu (about 10:08 AM) that protesters entered through eateries and food stalls, that a demonstration at Jantar Mantar is illegal because the site has been de-notified, and that they were detained immediately. That is the police account. Earlier account: RELEASED (~10 AM, 11 Oct).
