Ratna Singh posted at 1:03 AM: "Since morning no one knows where they are, their families don't have any idea, the lawyers have no clue." PTI (12:46 PM): Dipke said Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will hold a press conference at 2 PM at the Press Club of India and announce the next steps. The Wire (2:00 PM) quotes Saurav Das: "We are returning with full strength." His words. A journalist's X post at 1:30 PM described heavy police outside the Press Club; that post is unverified. The press conference was held at the Press Club of India on the afternoon of 11 Oct. Saurav Das (PTI, about 2:50–3:02 PM; Hindustan Times) said Delhi Police "forcefully entered" the airplane and "kidnapped" them, that there was no formal detention notice, that phones were seized with no seizure memo, and that they were not allowed a lawyer. He said he suspects the phones were "hacked or cloned." He said, "We will not go back," and appealed to citizens to take to the streets. On the one-year condition against a breach of the peace, he said the breach was done by PM Modi, Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar. He also said Delhi was "like a fort with 40,000 personnel" and that more than 50 metro stations were shut. Those are his figures and his words. Ashutosh Ranka (ThePrint) said, "The fight will continue until every single one of our demands is met." He thanked Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Manik Sarkar and Pinarayi Vijayan. He said several CJP colleagues were detained and assaulted on Sunday and that "the entire SFI team was detained today" (ANI, 3:10 PM). CNN-News18 reported that he said the fight is now also against PM Modi. His words. Ratna Singh spoke at the same briefing. The Hindu (3:38 PM) lists her among those released. ThePrint (3:50 PM) reported Delhi Police at the door of the Press Club while CJP was inside. PTI (4:27 PM) and ThePrint (4:53 PM) reported that the notices were fresh notices in an old case about a woman's allegedly morphed images circulated online, following Delhi High Court directions on her plea. CJP told NDTV (5:31 PM) that wrong tweets were attributed to them and that they will contest the notice. No fresh detention of Das, Ranka or Singh has been reported. Social posts claiming they ran from the Press Club are unverified; no news outlet has reported that. NDTV (5:56 PM): Ashutosh Ranka said, "The fight has just begun," and that it will not stop until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. Saurav Das said the protests would be "not just in Delhi but the whole country." CJP wants Jantar Mantar opened as a venue. Their words. On X at 8:51 PM he accused Delhi Police of "collaborating with these sexual assaulters." His claim. On 12 Oct he and Ashutosh Ranka reached Parliament Street police station around 11:36–11:52 AM (IANS, The Hindu, Hindustan Times, PTI). Das (ANI, 11:31 AM, and Hindustan Times, 11:49 AM): "Police tells everyone to approach them 10 days in advance. We are now saying that they have the choice to tell us the date and time ... We are giving them 24-hour ultimatum." He also said (IANS, 11:40 AM): "Peaceful protest is a right, a constitutional right, and people are already exercising it." His words. No police response was reported as of 12:10 PM. On the de-notification (PTI, about 2:52 PM, and Indian Express) he said: "Unacceptable. Why is Narendra Modi scared of Jantar Mantar? The Jantar Mantar belongs to the people of India. Did the Ministry of Home Affairs consult with the people of India? Were any stakeholders consulted? Were any organisations consulted?" He also said: "We do not accept this arbitrary decision. It is an assault on people's fundamental right to protest and peaceful assembly. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar ban raha he." His words. PTI (about 2:48 PM) shows him and Ashutosh Ranka submitting a letter to the DCP at Parliament Street seeking permission for a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. No date from police was reported as of 3:06 PM. As of 3:11 PM on 13 Oct, still no release was reported. CJP legal head Ratna Singh alleged that the SHO of Jaffarpur Kalan police station refused to let a lawyer meet Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and others, and that their phones were confiscated (her X post, about 12:39 PM; The Hindu, about 2:20 PM). Her claim. Hindustan Times (published about 12:59 PM, updated about 2:52 PM): CJP legal representative Pushp Sharma told PTI he has not been allowed to meet Das, Ranka and 12 others detained with them. He said the last WhatsApp from Das was that phones were being taken, and that the SHO told him the phones are "kept safe" and that he can call if needed. That is Sharma's account of the SHO. Police were not quoted responding to the lawyer-access or phone claims in these reports. Abhijeet Dipke (ETV Bharat, about 3:08 PM) claimed Ashutosh, Ajinkya and Saurav were held at separate locations, that 11 volunteers were taken elsewhere, and that lawyers were barred and threatened with further detention. He asked, "How can you arrest someone for hoisting the tricolour?" His claim. The Hindu (about 4:48 PM) reported CJP accusing Delhi Police of illegal detention and of denying access to lawyers, and calling for the release of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya and other members. That is CJP's accusation. Times of India (about 5:52 PM), citing ANI: Abhijeet Dipke said they were still in detention. He wrote, "Saurav, Ashu and Ajinkya are still in detention and the police is not allowing the lawyers to meet them," and, "How can police stop lawyers from meeting them? This is kidnapping because the police are certainly not following the rule of law." Speaking to ANI, he said he had just spoken to CJP legal head Ratna Singh, who told him the three had been kept separately, that 11 volunteers had been taken elsewhere, and that police did not let lawyers enter the station and threatened others with detention. That is Dipke's account of what she told him. Police were not quoted responding. No release was reported as of 6:10 PM. ANI (about 8:44–8:47 PM) said Delhi Police registered a case against Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others for "unauthorised trespassing through the house" over entering Jantar Mantar on 13 Oct. ANI's wording names Das and Ranka and "others." No reliable outlet confirmed a penal section, so none is stated here. An account @CJP_for_India, which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, posted at about 7:27 PM that the leaders had "not yet been released." Treat that post as unverified. No release was reported as of 9:15 PM.

Same as Dipke

That is CJP's argument. No bail order was reported as of 9:00 AM on 15 Oct. As of about 9:00 PM IST on 15 Oct, no bail order was reported. He remains in Tihar on the five days' judicial custody from 14 Oct. Times of India says the Special Executive Magistrate matter is still listed for further inquiry on 19 Oct. The Patiala House bail application reported on 14 Oct (India Today) had no grant or rejection in the reports checked today. India Today says he is in Tihar Jail No. 4, as an undertrial after medical checks. Earlier account: Held. Detained again on the morning of 13 Oct at Jantar Mantar, with Ajinkya Shinde (The Hindu, the Economic Times and Times of India; reports from about 9:48 AM). No release was reported as of 12:15 PM. Times of India quotes him: "Today 5 people entered… tomorrow 50,000 would enter until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. Protest will take place at Jantar Mantar only." His words. Das said they were taken to Jaffarpur police station (The Hindu, about 11:13 AM). A senior Delhi Police officer told The Hindu they entered through eateries and food stalls and that protesting at the de-notified site is illegal. That is the police account. Earlier account: RELEASED (~10 AM, 11 Oct). An Executive Magistrate ordered the release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:58 AM, citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench, 10:00 AM, which reports them released). This corrects earlier reports, including this page's 8:15 AM update, that they were still in custody. LiveLaw (10:20 AM), citing Ratna Singh, says they were released on condition they will not engage in a breach of the peace for one year. PTI (10:54 AM) says the condition is that they "maintain peace" for one year. Delhi Police, via ANI (10:56 AM), say the preventive arrest was under BNSS Sections 126 and 170 on 10 Oct 2026, that all due legal procedures were followed, that they were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate's court at Delhi Cantt, and that a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was taken. That is the police account. CJP counsel Soutik Banerjee said at 10:18 AM that all three had been released (LiveLaw). Indian Express (10:51 AM) says they walked out of Delhi Cantt police station. Delhi Police had placed the three under preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 (security for keeping the peace) and 170 (arrest to prevent the commission of cognisable offences) (LiveLaw, 8:23 AM; Bar & Bench, 8:32 AM; PTI, 9:10 AM; Indian Express, 9:34 AM). They were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate, South West District, at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:35 AM; Bar & Bench, 9:39 AM; ANI video, 9:51 AM). India Today (9:00 AM, police sources) had said that no arrests had been made. Earlier account: At 1:08 PM, intelligence sources told The Hindu that Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to three different locations in Delhi-NCR. CJP said at ~4:45 PM it still has no information on their whereabouts and is concerned for their safety. CJP said at a 7:35 PM press conference it still has no information on the whereabouts of Dipke, Das and Ranka (The Hindu). Police sources (The Hindu, 7:38 PM) say due legal process will be followed in the case of CJP leaders. Ajinkya Shinde (CJP, ~8:55 PM) alleges police did not let Dipke speak to his lawyer or family after news of his grandmother's death. CJP says Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to different locations across Delhi-NCR (The Hindu; IANS, 9:04 PM). SFI joint secretary Aishe Ghosh demanded their release (The Hindu, 8:35 PM). NDTV (~10 PM) says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remained in custody. Delhi Police sources (ANI, 9:38 PM): all detainees were released from detention centres except CJP leaders, and due legal process will be followed for the CJP leaders. 10:47 PM: Hindustan Times reports Delhi Police posted on X that Dipke was "immediately" told of his grandmother's death and the funeral time and was offered "possible facilitation" to travel home; CJP replied, "Where is Abhijeet? His family wants to talk to him... last rites tomorrow morning." 10:53 PM: CJP posted, "It's been 12 hours. No information. No accountability," and demanded immediate release, disclosure of whereabouts and access to lawyers for Dipke, Das and Ranka. HT (11:25 PM) says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee are still held while everyone else was released. NDTV says the four remained in custody as of 12:15 AM, and that everyone else among at least 3,000 detainees was released. Ajinkya Shinde wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner at 11:29 PM asking where Dipke, Das and Ranka are (IANS). A habeas corpus plea seeking their production and release was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. CJP legal cell chief Ratna Singh posted at 12:48 AM: "This petition is not filed by @Cockroachisback. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." CJP reposted that and added "Please note." Bar & Bench and LiveLaw report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. Ratna Singh posted at 1:03 AM: "Since morning no one knows where they are, their families don't have any idea, the lawyers have no clue." After release he wrote on X at 11:32 AM, in Hindi. The Wire's translation: Gyanesh Kumar is a "traitor" and he is ready to stay in jail for his entire life to get him removed. His words. PTI (12:46 PM): Dipke said Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will hold a press conference at 2 PM at the Press Club of India and announce the next steps. The Wire (2:00 PM) quotes Saurav Das: "We are returning with full strength." His words. A journalist's X post at 1:30 PM described heavy police outside the Press Club; that post is unverified. The press conference was held at the Press Club of India on the afternoon of 11 Oct. Saurav Das (PTI, about 2:50–3:02 PM; Hindustan Times) said Delhi Police "forcefully entered" the airplane and "kidnapped" them, that there was no formal detention notice, that phones were seized with no seizure memo, and that they were not allowed a lawyer. He said he suspects the phones were "hacked or cloned." He said, "We will not go back," and appealed to citizens to take to the streets. On the one-year condition against a breach of the peace, he said the breach was done by PM Modi, Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar. He also said Delhi was "like a fort with 40,000 personnel" and that more than 50 metro stations were shut. Those are his figures and his words. Ashutosh Ranka (ThePrint) said, "The fight will continue until every single one of our demands is met." He thanked Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Manik Sarkar and Pinarayi Vijayan. He said several CJP colleagues were detained and assaulted on Sunday and that "the entire SFI team was detained today" (ANI, 3:10 PM). CNN-News18 reported that he said the fight is now also against PM Modi. His words. Ratna Singh spoke at the same briefing. The Hindu (3:38 PM) lists her among those released. ThePrint (3:50 PM) reported Delhi Police at the door of the Press Club while CJP was inside. PTI (4:27 PM) and ThePrint (4:53 PM) reported that the notices were fresh notices in an old case about a woman's allegedly morphed images circulated online, following Delhi High Court directions on her plea. CJP told NDTV (5:31 PM) that wrong tweets were attributed to them and that they will contest the notice. No fresh detention of Das, Ranka or Singh has been reported. Social posts claiming they ran from the Press Club are unverified; no news outlet has reported that. NDTV (5:56 PM): Ashutosh Ranka said, "The fight has just begun," and that it will not stop until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. Saurav Das said the protests would be "not just in Delhi but the whole country." CJP wants Jantar Mantar opened as a venue. Their words. On X at 10:05 PM he wrote: "Unbelievable stories of police brutality coming out against CJP leaders. From tomorrow, not a single CJP leader will leave detention centres without proper MLC [medico-legal certificate]." That is his allegation. Delhi Police have not answered that post in the reports used here. On 12 Oct he and Saurav Das reached Parliament Street police station around 11:36–11:52 AM. Ranka (IANS and PTI): "We are going to ask Delhi Police for a date to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar. We hope the police will give us a date. If they do not, we will make another call within 24 hours." His words. No police outcome was reported as of 12:10 PM. PTI (about 2:48 PM) shows him and Saurav Das submitting a letter to the DCP at Parliament Street seeking permission for a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. No date from police was reported as of 3:06 PM. Hindustan Times (about 12:01 PM) quoted him saying the CJP team "will be there" in solidarity with the INDIA bloc march. As of 3:11 PM on 13 Oct, still no release was reported. CJP legal head Ratna Singh alleged that the SHO of Jaffarpur Kalan police station refused to let a lawyer meet Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and others, and that their phones were confiscated (her X post, about 12:39 PM; The Hindu, about 2:20 PM). Her claim. Hindustan Times (published about 12:59 PM, updated about 2:52 PM): CJP legal representative Pushp Sharma told PTI he has not been allowed to meet Das, Ranka and 12 others detained with them. He said the last WhatsApp from Das was that phones were being taken, and that the SHO told him the phones are "kept safe" and that he can call if needed. That is Sharma's account of the SHO. Police were not quoted responding to the lawyer-access or phone claims in these reports. Abhijeet Dipke (ETV Bharat, about 3:08 PM) claimed Ashutosh, Ajinkya and Saurav were held at separate locations, that 11 volunteers were taken elsewhere, and that lawyers were barred and threatened with further detention. He asked, "How can you arrest someone for hoisting the tricolour?" His claim. The Hindu (about 4:48 PM) reported CJP accusing Delhi Police of illegal detention and of denying access to lawyers, and calling for the release of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya and other members. That is CJP's accusation. Times of India (about 5:52 PM), citing ANI: Abhijeet Dipke said they were still in detention. He wrote, "Saurav, Ashu and Ajinkya are still in detention and the police is not allowing the lawyers to meet them," and, "How can police stop lawyers from meeting them? This is kidnapping because the police are certainly not following the rule of law." Speaking to ANI, he said he had just spoken to CJP legal head Ratna Singh, who told him the three had been kept separately, that 11 volunteers had been taken elsewhere, and that police did not let lawyers enter the station and threatened others with detention. That is Dipke's account of what she told him. Police were not quoted responding. No release was reported as of 6:10 PM. ANI (about 8:44–8:47 PM) said Delhi Police registered a case against Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others for "unauthorised trespassing through the house" over entering Jantar Mantar on 13 Oct. ANI's wording names Das and Ranka and "others." No reliable outlet confirmed a penal section, so none is stated here. An account @CJP_for_India, which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, posted at about 7:27 PM that the leaders had "not yet been released." Treat that post as unverified. No release was reported as of 9:15 PM.

Same as Dipke

Ratna Singh

Very importantReleased

Lawyer, head of CJP's legal cell

Time 10 Oct, morning (reported by about 9:15–10:26 AM IST)

Place Outside her home in Jangpura, Delhi. Kept inside a car

RELEASED. The Hindu (3:38 PM, 11 Oct) lists Ratna Singh among those released, and she spoke at the CJP press conference at the Press Club of India. This replaces the earlier conflicting-reports status. Hindustan Times: she alleged that police visited volunteers' homes and intimidated parents from Friday night into Saturday, and that she was followed by the Intelligence Bureau after landing in Delhi. Her allegation. ANI (3:58 PM): she said the release conditions were the standard template, with "no special conditions." Her words. Earlier account: Free — acting as CJP's lawyer at the 11 Oct production; earlier detention reports unconfirmed. ANI reported she was released (~5:53 PM), and Saket court dismissed her plea for an FIR and a release direction (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench, ANI, 5:53 PM). The Hindu live blog (8:13 PM entry) says she posted at 7:13 PM: 'I am still detained. Since 9AM. There are 30 police official for one woman.' The Hindu (8:32 PM) and The Wire (8:54 PM) report a Delhi court dismissed her plea alleging wrongful confinement by police outside her Jangpura home. The Wire quotes her: 'Judge Serving Master' and 'Welcome to new India, where Sarkar can put 30 police personnel confining you...' LiveLaw (9:26 PM): a Delhi court rejected her plea for an FIR against policemen for wrongful confinement and for restraining her from protesting. Neha Bora (AISA) posted at 9:14 PM, 'Why is @whattalawyer still under house arrest?' Attributed as Bora's claim. Status remains conflicting reports as of 10:05 PM. A habeas corpus plea filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity referred to her detention. She posted at 12:48 AM that the petition was not filed by CJP, that CJP is not approaching the Supreme Court, and that CJP's legal team did not approve it. Bharti has sought to withdraw it (Bar & Bench, LiveLaw). She was posting on X between 12:48 AM and 1:46 AM. No outlet has reported her detention status. At 8:02 AM she posted that she will be at Delhi Cantt Police Station at 9 AM, as CJP's legal head, with other advocates, for the production of Dipke, Ranka and Das before an Executive Magistrate. That is consistent with her being free to attend, but no outlet has confirmed her release. On the morning of 11 Oct she was at Delhi Cantt Police Station as CJP's legal head. LiveLaw and Bar & Bench cited her for the Executive Magistrate's release order. No outlet has published a separate confirmation of when her own detention ended. As of 10:05 AM. Her account of the leaders' release, via LiveLaw (10:20 AM), is that the magistrate's condition was no breach of the peace for one year. Dipke later said he had not signed any bond that says they will not protest. Both accounts are kept.

She says police had only 'oral orders from above' and showed no notification

As of 12:10 PM on 12 Oct, still no outlet has confirmed a release. As of 3:06 PM on 12 Oct, still no outlet has confirmed a release. Ajinkya Shinde

Released

CJP organisation in-charge, from Latur

Time Morning of 13 Oct 2026

Place Jantar Mantar, then Jaffarpur police station, according to Saurav Das (The Hindu, about 11:13 AM)

RELEASED (14 Oct) on personal bond. The same Special Executive Magistrate court at Mandir Marg released him on a personal bond of Rs 5,000 (Indian Express; ABP Live). Indian Express says the condition is that for one year he will not take part in activity that breaches the peace. ABP Live says six months. Both accounts are kept. Times of India (published 7:05 AM, 15 Oct) also says he was bound down to maintain peace and good behaviour for six months. Abhijeet Dipke (X, 14 Oct, via Moneycontrol) said the 11 other CJP activists detained with them were released: "Welcome back team." His post. Das and Ranka were not released. They were remanded to five days' judicial custody in Tihar. Earlier account: Held. Detained on the morning of 13 Oct at Jantar Mantar with Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka (The Hindu, the Economic Times and Times of India). No release was reported as of 12:15 PM. Dipke posted that they entered with the tricolour before police picked them up. His claim. Das said they had been inside and were being taken away, and later that they were at Jaffarpur police station. Ranka said the protest will take place at Jantar Mantar only. Their words. A senior Delhi Police officer told The Hindu (about 10:08 AM) that they entered through eateries and food stalls and that a demonstration there is illegal because the site has been de-notified. That is the police account. As of 3:11 PM on 13 Oct, still no release was reported. CJP legal head Ratna Singh alleged that the SHO of Jaffarpur Kalan police station refused to let a lawyer meet Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and others, and that their phones were confiscated (her X post, about 12:39 PM; The Hindu, about 2:20 PM). Her claim. Hindustan Times (published about 12:59 PM, updated about 2:52 PM): CJP legal representative Pushp Sharma told PTI he has not been allowed to meet Das, Ranka and 12 others detained with them. He said the last WhatsApp from Das was that phones were being taken, and that the SHO told him the phones are "kept safe" and that he can call if needed. That is Sharma's account of the SHO. Police were not quoted responding to the lawyer-access or phone claims in these reports. Abhijeet Dipke (ETV Bharat, about 3:08 PM) claimed Ashutosh, Ajinkya and Saurav were held at separate locations, that 11 volunteers were taken elsewhere, and that lawyers were barred and threatened with further detention. He asked, "How can you arrest someone for hoisting the tricolour?" His claim. The Hindu (about 4:48 PM) reported CJP accusing Delhi Police of illegal detention and of denying access to lawyers, and calling for the release of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya and other members. That is CJP's accusation. Times of India (about 5:52 PM), citing ANI: Abhijeet Dipke said they were still in detention. He wrote, "Saurav, Ashu and Ajinkya are still in detention and the police is not allowing the lawyers to meet them," and, "How can police stop lawyers from meeting them? This is kidnapping because the police are certainly not following the rule of law." Speaking to ANI, he said he had just spoken to CJP legal head Ratna Singh, who told him the three had been kept separately, that 11 volunteers had been taken elsewhere, and that police did not let lawyers enter the station and threatened others with detention. That is Dipke's account of what she told him. Police were not quoted responding. No release was reported as of 6:10 PM. ANI (about 8:44–8:47 PM) said Delhi Police registered a case against Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others for "unauthorised trespassing through the house" over entering Jantar Mantar on 13 Oct. ANI's wording names Das and Ranka and "others." No reliable outlet confirmed a penal section, so none is stated here. An account @CJP_for_India, which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, posted at about 7:27 PM that the leaders had "not yet been released." Treat that post as unverified. No release was reported as of 9:15 PM. He was detained with them on the morning of 13 Oct. ANI's line does not name him separately. As of about 9:00 PM IST on 15 Oct he remains released on that personal bond. No new detention was reported. Das and Ranka were still in Tihar. No bail order for them was reported.

Delhi Police say the group entered a de-notified protest site through eateries. CJP says they were inside protesting.

Notable people who joined / backed it

  • Ajinkya Shinde — RELEASED (14 Oct) on a personal bond of Rs 5,000. Indian Express says that for one year he will not take part in activity that breaches the peace. ABP Live says six months. His claim. No police confirmation was found as of 9:35 PM. On 14 Oct a Delhi court issued fresh summons in the 2018 defamation case over his "BJP IT Cell" video. The next hearing is 17 Oct (NDTV; New Indian Express). Separate from the protest case. ThePrint: he claims Delhi Police are following him in unmarked cars. His claim.   • Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Mallikarjun Kharge, KC Venugopal — Congress / INDIA bloc street protests, 6–9 Oct. 4:57 PM video: 'Keep protesting. We are proud of you' (The Hindu). NDTV (7:41 PM), quoting his X post: 'Arrest all the leaders... Arrest us all... Youth of India, I am proud of you. Keep protesting.' INDIA bloc leaders will meet CJI Surya Kant on Monday to submit a memorandum. Indian Express (9:41 PM): Monday's march starts at 1:30 PM from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba junction. Kharge says he and Rahul were given 4 PM to 5 PM on Monday to meet Chief Justice Surya Kant (PTI via ThePrint). That slot is Kharge's account. PTI (9:47 PM): he and Kharge have written to the Chief Justice seeking a 4–5 PM meeting on Monday. Demands they describe include a return to paper ballots. News9 (11:09 PM), citing people aware of the matter, says Chief Justice Surya Kant declined that 4–5 PM slot. K.C. Venugopal says the march is still on (ANI, via webindia123). On 12 Oct he left his residence around 11:49 AM for a press conference at Indira Bhawan (ANI; IANS, 12:03 PM). The press conference was not yet reported. The march is still set for 1:30 PM. At the Indira Bhawan press conference (about 12:17–1:30 PM) he said the bloc will file a Supreme Court petition rather than submit a memorandum. As of 3:06 PM the filing was not confirmed. The march toward the court was underway. Update, evening of 12 Oct: his lawyer, Advocate S. Prasanna, filed the Supreme Court petition on his behalf after he could not reach the court by the 4:30 PM filing cut-off (Economic Times, updated 4:56 PM; The Hindu, about 5:07 PM). India Today says the petition is registered on the Supreme Court website. No hearing date was confirmed. Police stopped the march at Bhagwan Dass Road. Evening of 12 Oct: after that filing he and other INDIA bloc leaders entered the Supreme Court from Gate B (Supreme Court Observer, 6:30 PM; Bar & Bench, about 7:08–7:55 PM). Diary No. 64196/2026. The Hindu (updated 8:52 PM) published the full co-petitioner and respondent lists. India Today (updated 8:29 PM) published ten prayers. They do not include removal of the Chief Election Commissioner. NDTV (updated 6:06 PM) reports registry processing aimed at a Tuesday hearing. That is not a cause-list confirmation. On a CJP question (Indian Express, about 8:21 PM) he said: "All protests are one, to remove Gyanesh Kumar." His words. Update, overnight: IANS, News18, India TV and DNA report 14 registry defects in Diary No. 64196/2026, including a Rs 220 fee shortfall and missing vakalatnamas for nine petitioners. Bar & Bench (11:43 PM) says the petition is not on the 13 Oct supplementary cause list. NDTV's likely-Tuesday report stays NDTV's report. PTI (12:41 AM, citing sources) says he will host a high tea for INDIA bloc MPs at his residence on Tuesday. BJP leaders allege he pushed a woman journalist on Monday evening. Supporters dispute that. No Congress response was found. PTI (8:26 AM, 13 Oct), citing sources, says INDIA bloc leaders will hold a joint press conference and that the tea at his residence now also includes civil society and student groups. On 14 Oct, on X: "Waving the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar in a peaceful protest is not a crime. Jailing youth for it is an act of cowardice." BBC also reported: "Students. Youth. Journalists. The INDIA bloc. Different banners, one cause. All protests are one: citizens demanding their constitutional rights." His words (India Today, 11:51 AM; BBC). On 15 Oct, about 8:27 PM, Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and K.C. Venugopal met NSUI, Indian Youth Congress and Seva Dal leaders at Indira Bhawan (The Hindu). Kharge said on X that the youth leaders had challenged what he called government authoritarianism. His words. The same day the Supreme Court issued notice on the INDIA-bloc SIR petition and, separately, NDTV reported notice to Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav on a plea against the 12 Oct court march.

Court updates

9 Oct · Supreme Court (CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana)

Called the transport notifications 'overreaching' and ruled out complete prohibition of metro and trains ('don't use a hammer to kill a fly'). The SG agreed authorities would reassess. Compliance reports due in 4 days. The court also said that protesting without permission can lead to prosecution. 1 · Supreme Court Observer

9 Oct · Delhi High Court

Refused an urgent hearing on the Youth Congress plea for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar. Listed for Mon 12 Oct. On 12 Oct, Justice Amit Mahajan began the hearing around 11:35–11:39 AM. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, for Delhi Police, sought time until tomorrow for instructions. The plea was adjourned to 13 Oct (Bar & Bench, 11:40–11:41 AM; LiveLaw, 11:40 AM and 11:48 AM). On 13 Oct, Indian Express (about 12:36 PM): before Justice Amit Mahajan, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma said the Indian Youth Congress plea for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar, filed for president Uday Bhanu Chib, had become "infructuous" after the site was de-notified. Senior advocate Siddharth Luthra, for Chib, said it was not infructuous, alleged "subterfuge", and said notice must issue and that they would amend the plea. The court passed the matter over, to take it up later the same day, with Luthra to appear in person. No final order was reported as of 3:11 PM. Later on 13 Oct, LiveLaw (6:08 PM): Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice on prayers (c), (d) and (f) and listed the matter for 17 Nov. Prayer (c) seeks a declaration that the 2022 standing order cannot impose an automatic ban on a peaceful assembly. Prayer (d) seeks a fresh, reasoned look at the protest request. Prayer (f) seeks a declaration that the 10-day application rule is not an absolute bar. Senior advocate Siddharth Luthra, for Uday Bhanu Chib, said he would amend the prayers after the de-notification and called conditions in the 2022 order bad in law. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma opposed notice. He said the petition is about demonstrating at Jantar Mantar, that the site was de-notified pursuant to Supreme Court orders, and that the petition cannot stand unless the de-notification is challenged. Notice on those three prayers is not an order granting permission to protest. 1 · Bar & Bench2 · X3 · X4 · X5 · The Hindu6 · Indian Express7 · LiveLaw

11 Oct · Supreme Court (special Sunday bench, 10:30 AM: Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana)

Menaka Guruswamy's plea is a habeas corpus petition. It challenges the detention of Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan, Manik Sarkar and other political leaders. To be heard on Sunday 11 Oct at the special sitting before Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana (LiveLaw). She told Bar & Bench that preventive detention cannot be used to suppress the right to peaceful protest. Bar & Bench (7:15 AM, 11 Oct): the bench assembles at 10:30 AM. Matters: Shailendra Mani Tripathi's contempt plea against Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chair D. Thara; Menaka Guruswamy's plea against preventive detention of opposition leaders, including four former chief ministers; and detention and alleged police excesses against lawyers, including Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat. Advocate Aman Prasad's contempt petition against the Delhi Police Commissioner is likely to be mentioned (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha has also moved the court the same morning seeking urgent directions (LiveLaw). At the hearing, which began about 10:32 AM, LiveLaw reported that the court restrained the virtual-hearing facility and then sat in Court No. 5; the virtual-hearing position was also described as a Webex meeting at full capacity, so that point is unclear. Bar & Bench named Kapil Sibal, Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Menaka Guruswamy, Arundhati Katju, Sanjay Hegde and advocate-on-record Anas Tanwir for the petitioners, and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta for the respondents. On K.K. Venugopal's contempt plea, Justice Bagchi said a similar petition was already before the court and proposed posting it to Monday; Venugopal asked for listing and replies, and the court said it would. At about 11:48 AM the bench said it will pass an interim order: the Metro should run normally unless a law-and-order situation arises, the public should have free movement, the internet should be restored, and lawyers should not be obstructed in their professional duties (LiveLaw). Bar & Bench quotes Justice Bagchi that no advocate should be hindered in discharging their professional duties, and that he summarised the Solicitor General as saying Metro services are normalised unless a public-order situation arises and that the internet is already restored. SG Tushar Mehta said all Metro stations are open today. India Today's live headline said barricades should be removed across Delhi and the internet cannot be shut down. LiveLaw's wording is the more precise account. From 12:03 PM Justice Bagchi was dictating the order (Bar & Bench). It records urgent applications alleging violation of the 9 Oct order and illegal detention on 10 Oct, and Dr Menaka Guruswamy's statement that GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya Metro stations, and others, were completely shut, which she called a deliberate and wilful violation (her allegation, as recorded). The state was asked to explain the circumstances, manner and justification of the detentions and to give station-wise Metro details on a map in its affidavit. Interim order passed (Bar & Bench, published 12:51 PM; the court rose about 12:36 PM). Metro and rail are to function normally unless regulation is needed for public order under Article 19(2). People may move freely in the city, subject to traffic regulations, and barricades are to be reviewed forthwith. The internet shall remain undisturbed, as per law; the order does not take away powers under the IT Act. No illegal detention except by procedure established by law. Peaceful assembly is to be permitted, particularly outside the area where Section 163 BNSS is in force. The Section 163 BNSS notice board near the Supreme Court is to be taken down. The court recorded an assurance that lawyers, journalists and other professionals will not be obstructed. A contempt notice was issued. The authorities are to file a short affidavit showing cause why contempt proceedings should not be initiated, plus a compliance report, including Metro restrictions and railway advisories, by Tuesday 13 Oct. Habeas corpus petitions on the mass detentions, and connected matters, are to be heard with the main cases on 13 Oct. The principal contempt petition is by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chair D. Thara (Bar & Bench). Justice V. Mohana asked those present to undertake to protest peacefully and not instigate others. Gopal Sankaranarayanan agreed, and asked for a matching undertaking on how police treat peaceful protesters. The court said the State must explain the circumstances, manner and legal justification of the detentions, and is duty-bound under Article 32. During the hearing the bench had proposed posting K.K. Venugopal's contempt plea to Monday. The reported order sets the next hearing for Tuesday 13 Oct. NDTV posted key takeaways at 1:50 PM. Written order uploaded at about 5:25 PM (LiveLaw PDF; Bar & Bench, 5:10 PM). The court finds a prima facie case of contempt over the alleged Metro and train shutdown, treated as a violation of its 9 Oct order. Notice was issued to the alleged contemnors. LiveLaw names Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, the Delhi Police Commissioner and the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation. They are to file counter-affidavits, including a compliance report, by 13 Oct. Personal appearance is dispensed with for now. Notice was also issued on the habeas corpus petition. Menaka Guruswamy argued that it covers illegal detention of about 7,000 people, not only named leaders. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta denied any violation. He said 45 of 303 Metro stations had been closed for law and order, denied that anyone was illegally detained, and called the habeas plea infructuous because detainees had been released. That is his submission, as recorded. The order directs that the Metro and trains run normally, subject to Article 19(2); that people move freely, with barricades reviewed forthwith; that the internet not be hindered; that there be no illegal detention of peaceful unarmed assemblies beyond the Section 163 BNSS area; and that the Section 163 notice board at the Supreme Court premises be taken down. Lawyers, journalists and other professionals shall not be hindered in any manner whatsoever. Listed again on 13 Oct with the other tagged petitions. 1 · X2 · X3 · X4 · X5 · Bar & Bench6 · X7 · X8 · Indian Express9 · LiveLaw10 · X11 · X12 · X13 · X14 · X15 · X16 · X17 · X18 · India Today19 · The Wire20 · Bar & Bench21 · X22 · X23 · LiveLaw24 · LiveLaw25 · X26 · X27 · X

11 Oct · Supreme Court (habeas corpus filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity; withdrawal sought)

Correction: this habeas corpus petition was filed under Article 32 by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, between about 11:39 PM and 12:10 AM. It was not filed by CJP, and CJP's legal team did not approve it. It sought production and release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others, disclosure of their whereabouts and the legal grounds for each detention, and preservation of CCTV footage, police diaries and movement registers. It asked whether the Section 163 BNSS order for Parliament Street can justify detentions at the airport and in Gurugram. It referred to the detention of Ratna Singh and other advocates and asked for their custodial status. It said it does not seek immunity from lawful action for any separate offence. Respondents named were the Centre, the Delhi government, Delhi Police, and Haryana, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh. Filed through advocates-on-record Rajesh G. Inamdar and Shashwat Anand. LawBeat says the plea also names Dhruv Rathee. Bar & Bench's report does not mention him (single source). At 12:48 AM Ratna Singh, CJP's legal cell chief, posted: "This petition is not filed by @Cockroachisback. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." CJP reposted that and added "Please note." Bar & Bench (12:46 AM and 12:58 AM) and LiveLaw (12:57 AM) report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. It is not described as listed with Menaka Guruswamy's separate habeas plea. Her plea is unaffected; no new report on it. 1 · Bar & Bench2 · X3 · X4 · X5 · X6 · X7 · X8 · X9 · X10 · X

11 Oct · Supreme Court (contempt; advocate Aman Prasad)

A new contempt petition against Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar was filed by advocate Aman Prasad (LiveLaw, 7:28 AM; Bar & Bench, 7:53 AM). He alleges police used "indiscriminate violence" against citizens on 10 Oct, in violation of Supreme Court principles. The petition says protesters near Jantar Mantar, INA and Dilli Haat were assaulted; a protester was lifted, thrown to the ground and beaten near INA; a young advocate who intervened when police allegedly pulled at a woman's trousers near INA was beaten, suffered head injuries and was taken to a hospital in Chhatarpur Enclave; women were manhandled by male officers; videos purportedly show a woman dragged by her hair in a detention bus and a woman journalist dragged across a road; Scroll's Ayush Tiwari was detained despite showing a press pass; officers were without name tags; and 45 of 57 metro stations were shut, with road blocks and a mobile-internet shutdown. It relies on the court's 28 July and 18 August orders and the 9 Oct order. LiveLaw says it is likely to be mentioned today, on Bar & Bench's 10:30 AM mentioning list. All of these are the petitioner's allegations. 1 · LiveLaw2 · X3 · X4 · X

12 Oct · Supreme Court (INDIA bloc march)

12 Oct: the INDIA bloc march will start at 1:30 PM from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba junction and go to the Supreme Court (Indian Express, 9:41 PM). Rahul Gandhi confirmed that time and place. At 9:32 PM he posted that students, civil-society groups and opposition parties should join a peaceful march to the Supreme Court. He and Mallikarjun Kharge are seeking to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice Surya Kant. Kharge told reporters they had written to the Chief Justice and had been given a slot between 4 PM and 5 PM on Monday (PTI via ThePrint). Kharge said, "We cannot demand anything before him (Surya Kant). We will request him with folded hands." That slot is Kharge's account, not a confirmation published by the court. Rahul says the memorandum demands an end to what he calls vote chori, a halt to the Special Intensive Revision, and Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. He alleged that young protesters on Saturday were beaten by police and by BJP workers. That is his allegation. He announced the march earlier on Sunday (Indian Express, 6:59 PM; PTI, 7:07 PM). PTI (9:47 PM): Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, Leaders of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, have both written to Chief Justice Surya Kant seeking a meeting between 4 PM and 5 PM on Monday to hand over a memorandum. The demands they describe include an end to what they call vote chori, Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, a halt to the Special Intensive Revision, and a return to paper ballots. Kharge, in Bengaluru, said: "We cannot demand. Only with folded hands, we can request him ... everywhere an undeclared emergency is imposed." His words. An earlier PTI report carried by ThePrint quoted him saying they had been given the 4–5 PM slot. Both wordings are his account. The court has not published a confirmation. News9 (updated 11:09 PM), citing people aware of the matter, says Chief Justice Surya Kant declined the 4–5 PM meeting. In an email reply he reportedly said the issues are already before the court, the court cannot meet political delegations at an administrative level, and they should file a petition. He stressed that the court's doors are open to everyone. That account is sourced to people aware of it, not to an official statement. K.C. Venugopal told ANI, via webindia123: "The CJI has declined to meet us, provided that open avenue for giving a petition to the Supreme Court by hand or a general legal way. We respect that decision, but we are very much for marching to the Supreme Court tomorrow." His words. The 1:30 PM march is still on. Indian Express (12:25 AM), reporting what it learnt, gives four points from the Chief Justice's reply: the SIR and CEC grievances are already pending; the court cannot take cognisance of them on the administrative side; if a petition is filed on Monday, Article 32 judicial review means it will be taken up on Tuesday 13 Oct with the matters already listed; and the court is committed to fundamental rights, with its doors always open. The 1:30 PM march from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba Road junction to the Supreme Court, about 2 km, is still on. The 4–5 PM meeting remains declined. On Monday morning, after the National Human Rights Commission's 33rd Foundation Day, Chief Justice Surya Kant told reporters (New Indian Express; Indian Express, 10:47 AM): "I received a letter yesterday regarding a meeting request, and I responded to it last night, outlining the reasons why I will be unable to meet." He also said: "The Supreme Court's doors are open to everyone. Any petition from any common citizen or member of an elected body is welcome. Every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court, and we will hear their concerns and grant whatever is due under the law." This is his own confirmation. Earlier accounts were from people aware of the matter. In open court, The Hindu's Krishnadas Rajagopal (11:36 AM) reported him saying that democratic and political protests need to take place, but the "Supreme Court should not be dragged into it" and "There should not be any inconvenience caused to litigants, lawyers, court staff." The 4–5 PM slot stays declined. The 1:30 PM march stays on. At the Indira Bhawan press conference (about 12:17–1:30 PM), Rahul Gandhi said the Chief Justice had instructed them to file a petition and that INDIA bloc leaders would go to the Supreme Court to file it, a shift from handing over a memorandum (New Indian Express, NewsDrum, India Today, The Hindu). India Today said the petition was planned for around 3 PM. As of 3:06 PM the filing was not confirmed in the wire copy used here. From about 2:30 PM to 3:05 PM the march was underway. Opposition MPs gathered at the Constitution Club, and a bus carrying Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and others went to the Barakhamba Road junction (PTI video, about 3:03 PM; ANI). The Hindu reported lawyers joining, and police formed a row before Congress protesters at Barakhamba around 2:25 PM. CPI's D. Raja (ANI) said MPs would march, and that inside the Supreme Court 10 leaders would sign the petition and submit it for the INDIA bloc, and that he is a signatory. That is the plan he described, not a report that the petition had been filed. Hindustan Times (about 12:01 PM) quoted CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka saying the CJP team "will be there" in solidarity. March coverage as of this check is INDIA-bloc-led. Update, evening of 12 Oct: the petition has been filed. Advocate S. Prasanna, Rahul Gandhi's lawyer, filed it on his behalf because Gandhi could not reach the court by the 4:30 PM physical-filing cut-off (IANS; Prasanna confirmed this to ANI, via the Economic Times, updated 4:56 PM). The legal team had first sought an extension of that 4:30 PM deadline from the Supreme Court registry (India Today, Zee News). India Today's live coverage says the petition is officially registered on the Supreme Court website. The Hindu (Krishnadas Rajagopal, about 5:07 PM) says it seeks an independent committee to inquire into the Special Intensive Revision and the Election Commission's decision-making on it, a re-look at online voter registration and services such as the ECINet portal, and an order calling for the Commission's records and official notings on the revision. The Hindu says the plea is also filed by Mallikarjun Kharge, Trinamool Congress MP Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and RJD's Tejashwi Prasad Yadav. Earlier, IANS via DNA, citing sources, said the court had agreed to let Gandhi and five to ten leaders, with lawyers, submit the petition at the filing counter outside the high-security area, and that the Chief Justice had agreed to that arrangement. That account is attributed to sources. No hearing date was confirmed in the reports used here. Evening update, as of 9:35 PM: after the 4:37 PM filing, Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders entered the Supreme Court from Gate B. Supreme Court Observer (6:30 PM) reported crowds chanting "Rahul Gandhi Zindabad" as he entered. Bar & Bench (about 7:08 PM, 7:38 PM and 7:55 PM) reported Delhi Police increasing security and trying to stop leaders, a registry that was shut at first, and later a crowd of lawyers and leaders, including Akhilesh Yadav and Supriya Sule, inside the registry. LiveLaw (about 7:24 PM) noted the writ had already been filed. The Hindu (updated 8:52 PM) and Supreme Court Observer: Diary No. 64196/2026, shown as filed at 4:37 p.m. through Advocate Prasanna S. Petitioners: Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Saugata Roy (TMC), Akhilesh Yadav (SP), Tejashwi Prasad Yadav (RJD), Supriya Sule (NCP-SP), Sanjay Raut (Shiv Sena UBT), D. Raja (CPI), Mahua Majhi (JMM), M.A. Baby (CPI-M) and E.T. Mohammed Basheer (IUML). Respondents: the Election Commission of India, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. India Today (updated 8:29 PM) published ten prayers: production of Commission files, notings, objections, ECINET/ERONET logs and the 24 June 2025 nationwide-SIR file; examination under Article 324, Section 18 of the 2023 Act and T.N. Seshan, and quashing of decisions taken without lawful authority; action including under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950; minuting under Section 18 while the case is pending; Form 6 to match the 1960 Rules unless those Rules are amended; an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge to audit deletions and database access and to review EVM practice; booth-wise publication of deletions with reasons and a gender and age breakdown; no deletion without notice and a hearing, with inclusion applications in Punjab and other poll-bound States until the last lawful date; interim suspension of the ongoing SIR; and other consequential orders. That prayer block does not ask for removal of the Chief Election Commissioner. The petition says it does not reopen the validity of SIR after ADR v ECI (27 May 2026). It challenges implementation and collective decision-making. It cites an Indian Express report of 23 September 2026 on objections inside the Commission, and notes the Commission's position that differences are normal and decisions were unanimous. NDTV (updated 6:06 PM) reports that the registry was directed to process the petition and rectify defects so it can be listed on Tuesday, and that a Chief Justice-led bench will likely hear it. NDTV does not name who gave that direction. It is not a published cause-list confirmation. Update, overnight into 13 Oct: IANS (about 11:04 PM), News18 and India TV (11:07 PM; India TV updated 11:47 PM) and DNA report that the registry notified 14 defects in Diary No. 64196/2026 on 12 Oct. The named defects include private individuals listed as respondents without explanation and discrepancies in respondent names; no copy of an earlier judgment annexed; vakalatnamas missing for nine petitioners, all except Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge; an illegible copy of Kharge's identity card; a Rs 220 shortfall in the court fee; and small-font, legibility and printing issues. DNA says the registry also asked for clear copies of the Election Commission's 24 June 2025 Special Intensive Revision decision and related records, and for digital copies on a pen drive. Under the Supreme Court Rules 2013 the defects must be cured before the matter can be listed. India TV says curing them all on Monday is likely to be difficult. Bar & Bench (11:43 PM) says Rahul Gandhi's petition does not figure in the Supreme Court's supplementary cause list for 13 Oct, released at 11:25 PM. Bar & Bench says the bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana is listed that day for CPI(M)'s M.A. Baby PIL, with a tagged contempt plea by Shailendra Mani Tripathi against Govind Mohan and Apoorvanand's plea; Menaka Guruswamy; RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha; the Association for Democratic Reforms; the Supreme Court Bar Association; SCAORA; the Youth Bar Association of India; and pleas by Priya Mishra, Samriddhi Das, who has sought an ex-parte stay, Bhanu Sanoriya, Mukesh Kumar Pandey, Aman Prasad and Anand Kumar Pandey. No report yet says the Gandhi petition's defects have been cured, or that it was mentioned or added to a later list. It could still be mentioned later. NDTV's earlier report that a Tuesday hearing was likely stays NDTV's report. Update, morning of 13 Oct: LiveLaw (8:01 AM and 9:05 AM) says the court will hear today the petitions challenging police and paramilitary action against the Delhi protesters, including allegations of mass illegal detention, assault and arbitrary metro shutdowns, before Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana. LiveLaw lists M.A. Baby of the CPI(M), Professor Apoorvanand, RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha, Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy, the Supreme Court Bar Association, SCAORA and others. That matches the Bar & Bench supplementary list. No outcome yet. The Gandhi petition's absence from that list is unchanged. PTI (7:50 AM) says the registry flagged more than 10 defects in the Gandhi petition. IANS, News18 and India TV said 14. Both counts are kept. Update, by about 12:05 PM: there was no full hearing on the merits, and no order disposing of the protest pleas. Indian Express (about 10:56–10:59 AM) reported that senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan mentioned a journalist's contempt plea, which these reports tie to Amaan Rastogi and the 11 Oct order. Chief Justice Surya Kant said matters can be listed once defects are cured, and "We will take up the matter tomorrow." The bench was the Chief Justice and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana. PTI and The Hindu (about 11:51 AM) and New Indian Express: the Chief Justice assured petitioners that all pleas related to the Delhi protests will be listed, and that they may be listed on Wednesday or Thursday. He said, "Make sure that the defects are cured." Indian Express (about 12:04–12:05 PM): the hearing was adjourned. The Chief Justice said Justice V. Mohana is unwell. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the affidavit and compliance report on the contempt notice are ready and that he wants them to be more comprehensive. The court extended the time to file the reply to the contempt notice. The Chief Justice also said listing will happen and that he would like some senior officer to remain present. BJP leader and senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia mentioned the previous day's incident at the Supreme Court, when opposition leaders were at the court. The court asked him to mention it tomorrow. Update, afternoon of 13 Oct: The Hindu and PTI (about 12:48 PM) and ETV Bharat report that the hearing on the Delhi-protest pleas, including detentions and the metro and train curbs, was deferred to Thursday 15 Oct 2026 because Justice V. Mohana was indisposed. The Hindu (about 1:36 PM): the Centre told the court its response on the alleged illegal detentions and the transport shutdown is ready but needs fine-tuning. The bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant extended the time to file that reply to Thursday 15 Oct. ETV Bharat paraphrased the Chief Justice as saying democratic activities must go on smoothly, but without obstructing the court's work or the movement of lawyers, staff and litigants. This Thursday date is for that protest-curbs and detention cluster. It is not a report that Rahul Gandhi's Special Intensive Revision petition was listed for 15 Oct. The defects in that petition still have to be cured. 1 · Indian Express2 · X3 · ThePrint4 · X5 · ThePrint6 · India Today7 · news9live.com8 · news.webindia123.com9 · newindianexpress.com10 · X11 · The Hindu12 · newindianexpress.com13 · newsdrum.in14 · India Today15 · X16 · X17 · X18 · X19 · X20 · NDTV21 · Hindustan Times22 · economictimes.indiatimes.com23 · zeenews.india.com24 · India Today25 · The Hindu26 · dnaindia.com27 · Supreme Court Observer28 · X29 · X30 · X31 · X32 · The Hindu33 · India Today34 · Bar & Bench35 · NDTV36 · NDTV37 · ianslive.in38 · news18.com39 · indiatvnews.com40 · dnaindia.com41 · X42 · X43 · X44 · ptinews.com45 · Indian Express46 · The Hindu47 · newindianexpress.com48 · etvbharat.com

12 Oct · BJP Mahila Morcha counter-march

12 Oct: the BJP Mahila Morcha announced a protest march against the Congress. It says the opposition is giving the protests political patronage (The Hindu, 7:25 PM). 1 · X

12 Oct · Madhya Pradesh High Court (Itarsi detentions)

A division bench of Chief Justice Alpesh Kogje and Justice Vivek Jain told the Narmadapuram Superintendent of Police to release or produce 18 people from Goa who were taken off a train at Itarsi. Next hearing Monday 12 Oct (Business Upturn, published 10 Oct, 8:13 AM). 1 · businessupturn.com

12 Oct · Bombay High Court, Goa bench (Azad Maidan detentions)

12 Oct, noon: the Goa bench continues the hearing. The Panaji and Pernem police station in-charges are to file affidavits on the reasons for the detention and on why the peaceful protest was not allowed (The Goan). On Sunday night the bench ordered the activists released. The Goan says they left Panaji police station around 9:40 PM. 1 · thegoan.net2 · X3 · Times of India4 · India Today

12 Oct · Supreme Court (SCBA plea on lawyer detentions)

Tuesday 13 Oct: the Supreme Court is to hear the Supreme Court Bar Association's petition on detention of lawyers and the internet suspension, and related pleas. Around 11:01 AM the Bar Association mentioned the petition before Chief Justice Surya Kant's bench (LiveLaw). Senior Advocate Nadkarni said a lawyer he represents has also filed (LiveLaw). IANS (11:18 AM): the Bar Association filed the petition and the hearing is tomorrow. PTI, via The Hindu (11:52 AM): a bench of Chief Justice Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana agreed to hear the petitions tomorrow, after Bar Association president Senior Advocate Pradeep Rai raised issues including internet restrictions. The Chief Justice said: "Democratic activities must take place smoothly, but there should be no obstruction to the functioning of the Supreme Court or movement of lawyers, court staff and litigants." PTI, via The Hindu (about 1:54 PM): the Chief Justice also said every lawyer has the right to participate in peaceful protests at designated locations, and the bench agreed to hear pleas against alleged police excesses tomorrow. 1 · X2 · X3 · The Hindu

12 Oct · Delhi High Court (listings for 13 Oct)

Three matters were listed for Tuesday 13 Oct. Justice Amit Mahajan's hearing of the Youth Congress plea for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar began around 11:35–11:39 AM. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, for Delhi Police, sought time until tomorrow, and the plea was adjourned to 13 Oct (Bar & Bench, 11:40–11:41 AM; LiveLaw, 11:40 AM and 11:48 AM). A plea challenging the closure of Jantar Mantar, saying no alternative site has been earmarked, was mentioned before the Acting Chief Justice's bench around 11:03 AM and listed for 13 Oct (LiveLaw, 11:03 AM; PTI, 11:21 AM; ANI, 11:35 AM). The Hindu (11:19 AM) says the High Court declined to hear it today because the Supreme Court is already seized of the matter. A separate plea alleging harassment of protesters by outsiders on 10 and 11 Oct will also be heard tomorrow (The Hindu). Acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambre agreed to list tomorrow an NSUI plea seeking a special investigation team into violence against protesters on 10 Oct (Bar & Bench, 11:12 AM). 1 · X2 · X3 · X4 · X5 · X6 · X7 · X8 · The Hindu

12 Oct · Delhi High Court (Mohammad Wasiq Nadeem Khan)

About 2:50 PM: PTI, via The Hindu, reported that the Delhi High Court asked city police to file a status report on civil rights activist Mohammad Wasiq Nadeem Khan's allegation that he was illegally detained to stop him attending a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. He also alleged constant surveillance and phone calls. A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma issued notice. Orally, the court acknowledged the police power to deny permission for a protest, and questioned entering his house and confining him: "How can you enter the house of this man? ... Where is your cause to confine him?" That is the allegation and the court's question. The status report is still to be filed. 1 · The Hindu

12 Oct · Supreme Court (Network of Women in Media, India)

Bar & Bench (9:57 PM, 12 Oct): the Network of Women in Media, India has petitioned the Supreme Court over the alleged detention, dragging and manhandling of journalists, including women reporters, covering the anti-CEC protests. The petitioners say police action continued despite the court's direction that journalists not be hindered. They seek binding safeguards and an independent inquiry. That is the petitioners' allegation. No police response was found in this check. No hearing date was reported. 1 · X

13 Oct · Supreme Court (Lawyers' Association for Constitution)

LiveLaw (published 7:40 AM) and Bar & Bench (9:04 AM): the Lawyers' Association for Constitution, convenor Senior Advocate Anjana Prakash, and advocates Fidel Tom, Sumita Hazarika, Anna Oommen and Anne Mathew have moved the Supreme Court under Article 32, through advocate-on-record Pyoli. LiveLaw spells the name Fidel Tom. Earlier cards on this page use Fidal Tom. They allege they were manhandled and illegally detained by Delhi Police on 10 and 11 Oct, and that Fidel Tom was assaulted in custody at Sanjay Colony police station and denied timely legal and medical help. They seek an independent, time-bound, court-monitored inquiry, which Bar & Bench says would be headed by a retired judge, plus preservation of CCTV, disclosure of detention records, mandatory name tags for police, compensation, rulings on the internet suspension, protection of journalists, and binding guidelines for policing peaceful assemblies. They invoke Articles 14, 15, 19, 21 and 22 and the D.K. Basu safeguards. Those are the petitioners' allegations. No police response was found. No hearing date for this petition, separate from today's already listed matters, was reported. 1 · LiveLaw2 · X

13 Oct · Supreme Court (Amaan Rastogi contempt plea)

LiveLaw (8:36 AM): journalist Amaan Rastogi, of Moliticis India, has moved the Supreme Court in contempt. He alleges repeated detention by Delhi Police on 10 and 11 Oct despite the court's order protecting journalists, and alleges manhandling, damage to his phone and destruction of his press identity card. Those are his allegations. No police response was found. No separate hearing date was reported. Update, morning of 13 Oct: Indian Express reported that senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan mentioned a journalist's contempt plea before the Chief Justice's bench. These reports tie that mention to this plea and to the 11 Oct order. The Chief Justice said it can be listed once defects are cured, and "We will take up the matter tomorrow." By about 12:05 PM the morning hearing had been adjourned, with Justice V. Mohana reported unwell, and the time to reply to the contempt notice was extended (Indian Express). No merits order was reported. Afternoon update: the protest-related sitting was later deferred to Thursday 15 Oct because Justice V. Mohana was indisposed (The Hindu / PTI, about 12:48 PM). These reports do not separately say Rastogi's contempt plea was given its own listing that day, beyond the morning remark that a journalist's contempt plea could be taken up once defects are cured. 1 · LiveLaw2 · Indian Express3 · The Hindu4 · etvbharat.com

13 Oct · Delhi High Court (protest SOPs and traders' losses)

The Hindu (Soibam Rocky Singh, about 11:10 AM): the Delhi High Court is to hear petitions seeking standard procedures to regulate protests and to limit disruption to businesses and lawyers. Senior Advocate Sachin Puri said recent protests caused losses exceeding Rs 2,000 crore to traders. That is his claim. The court was to hear the matter at the end of the board and was awaiting the Supreme Court's directions on related issues. No order was reported as of 12:15 PM. 1 · The Hindu

14 Oct · Special Executive Magistrate, Mandir Marg

Delhi Police placed Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde under preventive arrest and produced them before the Special Executive Magistrate at Mandir Marg. Das and Ranka were remanded to five days' judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail (Indian Express; The Hindu, updated 12:16 AM on 15 Oct; BBC, about 9:55 AM; AP). India Today says Das is in Jail No. 2 and Ranka in Jail No. 4. The Hindu: an FIR was registered under sections pertaining to breach of bond, criminal trespass and disobedience of orders, "among other charges" (officials). BBC says police accuse them of trespassing, breaching a peace bond, violating prohibitory orders and obstructing public officials, and that those are "charges they deny." Delhi Police, via Indian Express, said they were arrested for alleged repeated attempts to disturb public peace and to instigate others through social media, and that custody was ordered because of a serious apprehension that if released on bail they would again violate the law and instigate others. That is the police account. Shinde was released on a personal bond of Rs 5,000. Indian Express says he must not take part in activity that breaches the peace for one year. ABP Live says six months. Both accounts are kept. Times of India (published 7:05 AM, 15 Oct) says the court held that if Das and Ranka were released on bail "they will violate law, instigate others," and that the matter is listed for further inquiry on 19 Oct. The same report says Shinde was bound down for six months. As of 9:00 PM on 15 Oct, Das and Ranka were still in that custody. No bail order was reported. The further-inquiry listing of 19 Oct, as Times of India reported it, was unchanged. 1 · Indian Express2 · Indian Express3 · The Hindu4 · bbc.co.uk5 · apnews.com6 · Times of India7 · abplive.com8 · The Hindu

14 Oct · Patiala House Court

India Today (video, published 1:07 PM): the CJP legal team is moving Patiala House Court for bail for Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. The argument is that BNSS procedure was violated during the Special Executive Magistrate inquiry, and that the magistrate relied on conduct and social media posts. That is CJP's argument. No bail order was reported as of 9:00 AM on 15 Oct. As of 9:00 PM on 15 Oct, no bail order was reported. No grant and no rejection of that application was found in the reports used for this update. 1 · India Today2 · The Hindu

15 Oct · Supreme Court (CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi)

Rahul Gandhi v Election Commission of India, the INDIA bloc leaders' writ filed on 12 Oct, is on the 15 Oct cause list before Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi (PTI via Deccan Herald, 7:27 PM on 14 Oct; The Hindu; Business Today). The Hindu says Justice V. Mohana is not sitting on 15 Oct and that the regular three-judge bench "stands cancelled." Indian Express (6:47 AM) says the batch of petitions on the 10 Oct protest clampdown and transport shutdown is to be heard along with it. Moneycontrol (11:08 PM on 14 Oct) reported the plea was "unlikely" to be heard on 15 Oct. Both expectations are kept. The outcome was pending as of 9:00 AM. Prayers, as reported from the petition: records of Election Commission decisions on SIR, ECINET and ERONET access logs, an independent audit of deletions by a committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, booth-wise publication of deleted names with reasons, no deletion without notice and a hearing, and an interim suspension of SIR nationwide. Those are the petitioners' demands. Outcome, 15 Oct: the bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice to the Election Commission, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi (LiveLaw, 12:55 PM; NDTV; Indian Express). LiveLaw also reported notice on Asaduddin Owaisi's SIR plea, and that when counsel pressed an interim prayer the court said notice was being issued on all the prayers. No interim stay or suspension of SIR was reported. Indian Express reported notice on modification of Form 6. The Hindu's 12:59 PM line also referred to Digvijaya Singh's petition. The Chief Justice said notice does not condone conduct and that one petitioner must explain it. Indian Express: "We are issuing notice, but we are not condoning the conduct." NDTV: "We will issue notice but we want to know his conduct on the next date of hearing." LiveLaw said similar SIR matters are on for Tuesday. Separate notices the same day, on the 12 Oct march, the Jantar Mantar de-notification, prohibitory orders and related pleas, are in the following cards. 1 · Indian Express2 · The Hindu3 · deccanherald.com4 · Business Today5 · moneycontrol.com6 · LiveLaw7 · Indian Express8 · NDTV9 · The Hindu

15 Oct · Supreme Court (CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi) — notice on the 12 Oct march

The Hindu (12:59 PM): notice on Digant Mishra's petition seeking criminal contempt against Rahul Gandhi for leading a "political procession" into the Supreme Court. Senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia, for the petitioner, said the attempt was to browbeat the judiciary. Chief Justice Surya Kant: "nobody can browbeat the judiciary." NDTV quoted him calling the attempts "feeble": "These are feeble attempts that nobody takes note of... we are not sitting in an ivory tower." NDTV reported notice to Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and others, and an order to preserve CCTV from the court premises for the 12 Oct protest. The Hindu (1:05 PM): the bench directed preservation of CCTV, including inside the apex court premises. Indian Express reported a direction to preserve all CCTV of the protests. Notice is not a conviction. 1 · The Hindu2 · NDTV3 · Indian Express4 · ndtvprofit.com

15 Oct · Supreme Court (CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi) — Jantar Mantar de-notification

Notice on a petition challenging de-notification of Jantar Mantar. The Hindu (1:01 PM) names the petitioner as Swaty Singh. Indian Express names advocate Swaty Malik, represented by senior advocate Mukta Gupta, a former Delhi High Court judge. The court asked the Union of India and the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, to file replies (Indian Express; NDTV Profit). Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said a committee had been constituted before the decision (NDTV Profit). Justice Bagchi said the court must examine whether "oral observations" can be construed as law, because the government affidavit had linked the move to the 9 Oct order, and that the requirement that protesters be "heard" must also be understood from the perspective of technology (Indian Express). Mukta Gupta said protesters must be heard near the centres of power (The Hindu). Police have named Burari Ground, Ramlila Ground or Ramlila Maidan, and CBD Ground. Notice is not an order restoring the site. 1 · The Hindu2 · Indian Express3 · ndtvprofit.com

15 Oct · Supreme Court (CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi) — prohibitory orders, journalists, contempt affidavits

Justice Bagchi, about 1:59 PM (The Hindu): notices on all the petitions; the Union is to file counters; reasons for the Sec 163 BNSS orders were sought; a response was sought on allegations of assault on protesters, lawyers and journalists. On the Delhi Union of Journalists' device plea, the Solicitor General denied seizures and was asked to say so in the counter. Those assault claims are the petitioners'. The denial is the Solicitor General's, not yet a finding. Indian Express: he also said anyone with a mobile phone is being treated as a journalist. The Chief Justice said everybody acting as a journalist will create problems (The Hindu, 1:33 PM). Indira Jaising, for the Network of Women in Media, sought an independent committee. The Hindu: the Chief Justice prima facie agreed to a committee of women members and a woman chair, with names to be suggested in sealed cover. The court said no coercive action against the woman journalist booked after she alleged police harassment. The Hindu describes the booking as following allegations of humiliation and casteist slurs. Indian Express, reporting Jaising, describes an FIR under the SC/ST Act and a complaint against an officer that was not registered. Both accounts are kept. Justice Bagchi said the court will examine whether freedom of expression lets every citizen claim to be a journalist. Notice also on street-vendor compensation pleas and on Bhanu Sanoriya's plea that organisers take responsibility for harm to others. Gopal Sankaranarayanan said that cuts both ways, including for the Police Commissioner (The Hindu; Indian Express). On contempt, Home Secretary Govind Mohan and Commissioner Anurag Kumar filed affidavits with "unconditional and unqualified apology" language while defending the 10 Oct measures as proportionate and intelligence-based (Indian Express; LiveLaw; The Hindu). The Solicitor General said the apology opening is standard and was misread (The Hindu, 12:57 PM). NDTV Profit: the court treated an apology with a justification as qualified. At 6:07 PM the Home Ministry said the opening apology is the mandatory form of a contempt reply (The Hindu). 1 · The Hindu2 · Indian Express3 · Indian Express4 · LiveLaw5 · ndtvprofit.com6 · India Today

15 Oct · Delhi High Court (Acting CJ Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma)

About 4:44–5:36 PM: refused to restrain CJP and Abhijeet Dipke from the proposed 16 Oct gathering at Central Park, Connaught Place. Did not grant express permission. The petitioner was a Palika Bazar street vendor seeking regulation, citing festive-season business loss and arguing that Connaught Place is not a designated protest site (India Today; The Hindu). Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma said steps were already in hand to control CJP's activities and that all possible legal measures would regulate the gathering, and that the petitioner's concerns would be addressed. The court recorded that assurance. When counsel pressed for a specific restrain order, the bench said: "Don't insist. We have passed the order." Listed for further consideration on 3 Nov 2026 (India Today). The refusal to restrain is not permission to occupy Central Park. NDMC later closed the park for 16 and 17 Oct, and Delhi Police issued the evening statement on a select group. Those are separate from this order. 1 · The Hindu2 · The Hindu3 · India Today
